SOURCES (web): Rise of Nations diplomacy — https://riseofnations.fandom.com/wiki/Diplomacy ; Sins of a Solar Empire diplomacy/pacts — https://sinsofasolarempire.fandom.com/wiki/Diplomacy_System and https://sinsofasolarempire.fandom.com/wiki/Pacts ; Stellaris diplomacy — https://stellaris.paradoxwikis.com/Diplomacy ; Warcraft 3 shared control/diplomacy — https://www.hiveworkshop.com/threads/warcraft-diplomacy.301050/ ; kingmaking analysis — https://www.skeletoncodemachine.com/p/is-kingmaking-cursed and http://www.diva-portal.org/smash/get/diva2:1876522/FULLTEXT01.pdf ; CoH teamplay — https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3354065356

=== ENGINE INTEGRATION MAP (where each piece lands) ===

1) RELATIONSHIP MUTATION ORDER. Add a synced Order 'SetPlayerRelationship' (offerer, target, proposedType) and 'RespondToOffer' (accept/decline), resolved in an IResolveOrder trait on the Player actor (pattern like existing player-actor traits). Handler recomputes AlliedPlayersMask/EnemyPlayersMask (OpenRA.Game/Player.cs:92-93) via the existing Union pattern from CreateMapPlayers.cs:149-171. Because masks are public LongBitSet, this is a few lines. Do it ONLY inside Tick (synced).

2) AGREEMENT STATE. New trait on the Player/World actor, e.g. DiplomacyManager (TraitInfo<DiplomacyManager>), holding a list of Agreement records {playerA, playerB, AgreementType enum, int expiryTick, flags}. ITick decrements toward expiry and on expiry issues the downgrade. AgreementType = {Ceasefire, NAP, Alliance, DefensivePact, TradeRoute, VisionShare, Vassal}. This is the 'controller that writes the old mask fields' — existing combat/path/vision code (AutoTarget.cs, Locomotor.cs:507, Shroud) keeps reading masks unchanged, preserving determinism.

3) OPINION (AI + minors). Integer field per (evaluator, other) on DiplomacyManager. Mutated only by deterministic events via the INotify family: gifts (+), being attacked (-- via INotifyDamage/INotifyKilled), shared enemy (+), broken treaty (-- and also a separate persistent Trust field). AI accept rule: opinion + offerValue > threshold(scaled by AI's relative score). All integer — satisfies lockstep ban on float/Random.

4) MINOR FACTIONS. A neutral Player (NonCombatant) owns city-state actors carrying a new MinorFaction trait (loyalty<Player> dictionary, integer) plus ProximityCapturable (already exists: ProximityCapturableBase.cs) and/or a 'bribe' interaction (spend credits order). Highest-loyalty player becomes allied with the minor (mask update); rewards delivered via existing GrantCondition / Production / cash traits. This is THE component that makes diplomacy live in 1v1 and skirmish-vs-AI.

5) UI. Portrait radial: extend the in-game player list / observer widgets; reuse ProductionPaletteWidget.cs icon-grid + the support-power cooldown ring for timers. Offer toasts via the existing notification/tooltip chrome. A Diplomacy lobby option gates the feature (add to lobby like other game options).

6) LUA / TESTABILITY FIRST. DiplomacyProperties.cs currently exposes only IsAlliedWith — extend it with SetRelationship / Offer / GetOpinion so map scripts and unit tests can drive the whole system headless before any UI exists (matches the project's lint/test-first culture; run make tests / make check).

=== AGREEMENT CHEAT-SHEET (payloads & tuning intent) ===
- Ceasefire: short (~60s) mutual no-auto-target truce; cheapest; buys breathing room. Break = instant, low Trust cost.
- NAP: medium (~3min) 'won't attack, no bonuses'; the default neutral-plus; mild Trust cost to break with telegraph.
- Alliance: shared vision + shared CONTROL (WC3-style permission flag, no ownership change) + see partner's production; capped to 1-2 per player; high Trust cost + telegraphed grace window to break. THE marquee feature.
- Defensive Pact: if partner is attacked you auto-enter war with the aggressor; the anti-gang deterrent.
- Trade Route: +X credits/min to both while a physical convoy/link survives; raidable → new tactical objective.
- Vision Share: one-way or mutual shroud reveal; cheap intel trade; great for scouting economy.
- Vassal/Protectorate: weaker player routes a % income to protector + protector gains limited control; protector pledges defense; the comeback/anti-elimination mechanic that keeps near-dead players in the match instead of kingmaking.

=== THE PSYCHOLOGY OF BETRAYAL (why this is the fun engine) ===
Breakable-but-binding promises create the only emotion an RTS economy can't: interpersonal tension. The design rule is surprise-WITH-counterplay: betrayal is always allowed (preserves drama), always telegraphed to the victim with a short grace window (so it's a timing/skill play, not a free hit), and always priced via a persistent Trust stat that minors and AI remember (so it's a gamble with a cost, not a dominant strategy). This mirrors why WC3 Diplomacy is beloved and why board-game Diplomacy generates legendary stories — without importing their slow pace. Time-boxing every pact means trust must be continually RE-extended, so the betrayal tension is recurring, not one-shot.

=== ANTI-PATTERN GUARDRAILS (summary) ===
Kingmaking → vassalage keeps losers invested; disable gifting to non-allies; disable diplomacy on ranked 1v1. Ganging → Defensive Pacts auto-punish pile-ons. Stalemate-by-alliance → time-box + decay + war-restlessness + max-alliance cap; permanent peace impossible. Menu-fest → fixed templated offers, one-click radial, hover-itemized opinion, no free text, no multi-step votes. Dintegration with balance → tune trade/tech-minor numbers alongside economy/tech work, not after.

research-eras.executiveSummary: Recommend a three-layer research system that is fast, legible, and real-time: (1) ERAS — 3 to 4 shared "tech eras" (Present Day → Networked → Autonomous → Near-Future) that act as Age-of-Empires-style gates: each era unlock is one big timed/paid decision that raises the ceiling for everyone, creating the core teching-up-vs-spending-now tension. (2) DOCTRINE — a one-time, irreversible branching fork per match into Econ / Military / Defense / Diplomacy-Intel specialization (Company-of-Heroes commander model), giving each player a strategic identity without a 100-node tree. (3) UPGRADES — a SMALL handful of mutually-exclusive, dramatic, readable per-era choices (drone swarm vs hypersonic vs laser-defense vs cyber) that change HOW a unit fights, never invisible +1/+1 stat taxes. The whole thing maps onto OpenRA's existing prerequisite + condition + support-power traits with essentially ONE new trait (a timed, paid research queue that emits a prerequisite). Hard rules: never more than ~5 live choices on screen at once (progressive disclosure), every choice must be a visible qualitative change, and "tech up" must always compete with "spend now" for the same dollars and the same build time. The Codex (encyclopedia) hangs off every node to surface the real-world ore/tech grounding without cluttering the decision UI.
keyFindings: The single most-cited failure mode in RTS research is the MANDATORY UPGRADE: StarCraft's +1 weapon/+1 armor are 'not creating any fun decisions, just another gate before you can use your unit.' They are invisible numerical taxes everyone always buys in the same order. The design literature is unanimous: if every good player researches it every game in the same order, it is not a decision — delete it or replace it with a fork.

The best in-match research creates DRAMATIC, READABLE, OFTEN MUTUALLY-EXCLUSIVE changes. Praised examples: Grey Goo's railgun turning a single-target attack into AoE; Dawn of War's Mark of Khorne vs Tzeentch fundamentally re-roling a squad; Universe at War letting you pick only 6 of 12 upgrades so specialization is forced. The test is 'does this open a strategic path' not 'does this add a number'.

AGES/ERAS (Age of Empires, Rise of Nations) are the cleanest way to get strategic depth with low cognitive load: a small number of big, paid, timed gates. Advancing is a real opportunity-cost gamble (you go army-light while you tech), and it RAISES THE CEILING rather than handing you a flat bonus. Rise of Nations adds the twist that WHICH branch you advance first encodes your strategy — exactly the Civ-like choice the user wants.

BRANCHING beats LINEAR for the 'meaningful choice' goal, but only with FEW forks. The Game Studies analysis: complex prerequisite chains give 'a reason to choose one path over the other instead of flailing about randomly,' but trees feel deterministic when there are too many nodes and only one real order. The fix is a handful of OR-gated big forks, not hundreds of AND-gated small ones.

COMPANY OF HEROES' commander/doctrine model is the proven template for branching specialization inside a fast RTS: you pick ONE doctrine, it's irreversible for the match, abilities unlock over time via Command Points, and the 3-way choice exists specifically 'to respond to what your opponent is doing.' This gives a strategic identity (the user's per-faction differentiation) without a research screen the player has to babysit.

Cognitive-load research is blunt: 4–6 options max per decision point, progressive disclosure ('show 3 critical settings + an Advanced toggle, not 50'), or players freeze. A deck/limited-availability interface lets players avoid memorizing giant trees. This caps the design: never show the whole future tech tree at once — reveal the next era's choices only when you reach it.

The contemporary setting maps PERFECTLY onto eras because real military tech has clear generational steps: Present Day (precision munitions, MANPADS, 4th-gen armor) → Networked/EW era (drones, GPS/satellite ISR, cyber, jamming) → Autonomous era (drone SWARMS, loitering munitions, AI targeting, the US 'Replicator' thousands-of-drones concept) → Near-Future (hypersonics Mach 5+, directed-energy/laser point defense, layered missile defense). Each era is a real, legible capability jump — ideal for big readable upgrade forks.

OpenRA can already express ~90% of this DATA-DRIVEN. ProvidesPrerequisite + TechTree + GrantConditionOnPrerequisite + the condition system + SupportPower/SupportPowerManager already do gated unlocks, conditional stat/ability changes, and timed off-map powers. The ONLY genuinely new piece is a 'research queue' trait: a player-actor trait that spends cash + time, then emits a prerequisite string (and/or grants a condition) when complete. Everything downstream (units, upgrades, doctrines, eras) keys off that prerequisite exactly like building prerequisites do today.
recommendations: ADOPT A THREE-LAYER MODEL, not one tech tree. Layer 1 = ERAS (shared, vertical, paced). Layer 2 = DOCTRINE (one irreversible branching fork). Layer 3 = ERA UPGRADES (a few mutually-exclusive readable picks per era). This is the whole system. It deliberately mirrors AoE ages + CoH doctrines + Universe-at-War limited-pick, which are the proven-good patterns, and avoids the StarCraft stat-tax pattern entirely.

LAYER 1 — ERAS: 3 forks for a fast game (Present Day → Networked → Autonomous → Near-Future = 4 tiers, 3 advancement decisions). Advancing costs significant cash AND a chunk of time during which you produce nothing else, researched at a single 'Command HQ / R&D' building. Advancing raises the ceiling (unlocks the next units/buildings and the next era's upgrade fork) rather than giving a flat buff, so the tension is always 'tech up now and be army-light, or stay this era and out-mass them.' Gate each era behind a built structure prerequisite so it also costs map/board commitment, RoN-style.

LAYER 2 — DOCTRINE: at the start (or at first era-up) each player commits irreversibly to ONE of four paths — Economy, Military, Defense, Diplomacy/Intel — Company-of-Heroes style. The doctrine slowly unlocks 3–5 doctrine perks over the match (timed or earned), is the main vehicle for the user's 'unique troop + unique building per country' requirement (a country's doctrine table is its identity), and is what makes diplomacy/EW/defense first-class strategic axes instead of an afterthought. Show all four up front (it's the ONE big legible choice); reveal the perks progressively as they unlock.

LAYER 3 — ERA UPGRADES: per era, offer ~2–4 BIG mutually-exclusive forks that change HOW something fights, never a +1. Examples grounded in real tech: 'Drone Swarm doctrine' (cheap massable loitering munitions) vs 'Hypersonic strike' (one expensive deep-strike support power) vs 'Directed-Energy point defense' (laser turrets that hard-counter the swarm) vs 'Cyber/EW package' (jam enemy production/vision for a window). Cap it: at most ONE upgrade fork is open at a time per production category. The counter-triangle (swarm beats armor, lasers beat swarm, cyber beats networked anything) is itself the strategic game.

ENFORCE THE 'NO INVISIBLE TAX' RULE in lint/review: if an upgrade only changes a number and every player would always buy it, it must be folded INTO the era unlock (so it's automatic and free, not a chore) or rebuilt as a mutually-exclusive fork. Reserve player decisions for choices that are visible on the battlefield. This directly fixes the #1 thing players hate about RTS research.

MAKE 'TECH vs SPEND' A SHARED RESOURCE CONTEST. Research must draw on the SAME pool as production (cash) and ideally the same build slot/time, so teching is never free background progress — it's always at the cost of units on the field right now. This is what converts research from a checklist into a real-time gamble. Optionally add a small dedicated 'research throughput' that doctrine-Economy/Research players can boost, so speccing into tech is itself a strategic identity.

USE PROGRESSIVE DISCLOSURE RUTHLESSLY: at any moment the player should see at most ~5 actionable research choices: the current era-up button, their unlocked doctrine perks, and the 1–2 open upgrade forks for what they're currently building. The full future tree lives in the CODEX (read-only, for planning and real-world flavor), not in the active HUD. This keeps it real-time-fast and avoids the decision-paralysis the cognitive-load literature warns about.

BUILD IT ON EXISTING ENGINE PRIMITIVES + ONE NEW TRAIT. Reuse ProvidesPrerequisite / TechTree / GrantConditionOnPrerequisite / the condition system / SupportPower. Add a single new player-actor trait — call it 'ResearchQueue' — modeled on ProductionQueue: it takes cost + time, and on completion calls into the prerequisite/condition system to emit an era/doctrine/upgrade token. Eras, doctrines, and upgrades then become pure MiniYAML data (prerequisite strings + conditions + support powers), validated by the existing Lint rules at build time. Minimal C#, maximal data-driven, fully deterministic (integer cash, integer tick timers — no floats/DateTime/Random in the tick path).
risks: TECH-UP DEATH SPIRAL: if advancing an era is too slow or too expensive, a rushing opponent kills you while you're army-light, and the dominant strategy becomes 'never tech, just mass tier-1.' Mitigate by tuning era cost/time so a defended player can survive one timing push, and by giving the Defense doctrine cheap early walls/point-defense so teching is protectable. Playtest the era timings first — this is the single most balance-sensitive number in the design.

SNOWBALL / RUNAWAY LEADER: eras raising the ceiling means a player one era ahead can be 'impossible to defeat if the gap is wide enough' (RoN's own words). In a 1v1 this can be unfun. Mitigate with hard counters that cross eras (a present-day MANPADS/AT ambush can still kill a near-future asset), keeping era jumps to 3 (not 6+), and making higher eras about new OPTIONS/roles more than raw stat dominance.

DOCTRINE BALANCE & THE 'ONE BEST DOCTRINE' TRAP: irreversible doctrine choice is only fun if all four are viable; if Military always wins, the choice collapses to a non-decision (the same failure as mandatory upgrades, one level up). Requires careful per-faction balancing and probably a counter-relationship between doctrines. High art/balance cost — this is where most of the tuning effort will go.

ART CEILING DOMINATES SCOPE: every distinct unit a fork unlocks needs 32-facing 2D sprite art, the user's stated main cost ceiling. Favor forks that re-skin/re-stat or re-arm EXISTING units (cheap: new projectile, new condition, new weapon) over forks that demand brand-new unit art. Hypersonics/cyber/EW/laser-defense can largely be support powers and weapon swaps on existing chassis — keep the truly new sprites for the marquee per-country unique unit.

DETERMINISM REGRESSION: the new ResearchQueue trait runs in the synced tick path; any float, wall-clock, or Random there causes multiplayer desync (the #1 OpenRA bug class). Must use integer cash + integer tick countdowns and mark synced fields [Sync], exactly like ProductionQueue. Code review must specifically check the research tick path for nondeterminism.

OVER-SCOPING INTO GRAND STRATEGY: diplomacy + research + intel + eras risks drifting toward the 'super-slow' Stellaris feel the user explicitly rejected. Guardrail: every research action must resolve in seconds-to-low-minutes and must visibly change the battlefield, not open sub-menus of sub-menus. If a system can't be explained as 'pay X, wait Y, now Z is different on the map,' it's too grand-strategy for this game.

CODEX BECOMING BUSYWORK/DISTRACTION: surfacing real ores and real tech is great flavor but must never be required reading to play. Keep the Codex strictly optional and asynchronous (open it between matches or while paused in skirmish); never gate a decision behind reading it, or it becomes the homework the cognitive-load research warns against.

precedents.name: Age of Empires II / Rise of Nations — Ages
precedents.whatTheyDid: Gate progress behind a small number of big, paid, timed 'age' advancements researched at a central building; advancing unlocks the next tier of units/buildings/upgrades. Rise of Nations adds four parallel research branches where WHICH you advance first signals your strategy.
precedents.outcome: Genre-defining and durable. The opportunity cost of advancing (you go economy/army-light while teching) is a celebrated source of tension; choosing your advancement order is a real strategic decision.
precedents.lessonForUs: This is the backbone — Layer 1. Few big gates beat many small nodes for legibility. Steal RoN's idea that the ORDER of advancement encodes strategy. Keep it to 3 advancements for a fast game.

precedents.name: Company of Heroes 1/2 — Doctrines / Commanders
precedents.whatTheyDid: Players commit to ONE of three doctrines per match (irreversible), unlocking ~3–5 mostly-active abilities over time via Command Points, explicitly to respond to the opponent. Each faction has its own doctrine set.
precedents.outcome: Hugely influential; gives every match a strategic identity and a mid-game 'what do I unlock now given what they're doing' decision without a research screen to micromanage. (CoH2's design also drew criticism when doctrines were paywalled/too numerous — keep the set small and free.)
precedents.lessonForUs: This is Layer 2 — the branching econ/military/defense/diplomacy fork and the vehicle for per-country identity (unique troop + building). Irreversible + slowly-revealed = strategic depth with near-zero ongoing UI burden.

precedents.name: StarCraft / StarCraft II — weapon & armor upgrades
precedents.whatTheyDid: Structure-based research that adds invisible +1 weapon/+1 armor stat increments that every competitive player buys in the same order every game.
precedents.outcome: Widely cited as the canonical example of a NON-decision: 'mandatory research isn't creating any fun decisions, just another gate.' Balance hinges on numbers players can't even see.
precedents.lessonForUs: The anti-pattern to avoid. Any upgrade that everyone always buys in the same order should be made automatic-on-era-up (free) or rebuilt as a mutually-exclusive fork. Reserve player choice for visible, qualitative changes.

precedents.name: Universe at War — limited-pick tech paths
precedents.whatTheyDid: Offered 12 possible upgrades across three tech paths but let the player research only 6, forcing specialization and trade-offs.
precedents.outcome: Praised for creating faction-defining specialization and genuinely meaningful trade-offs — you can't have everything, so your tech loadout is a strategic statement.
precedents.lessonForUs: Apply the 'pick N of M' constraint to Layer 3 era upgrades. Scarcity of picks is what turns upgrades from a checklist into a decision. Combine with mutually-exclusive forks for maximum readability.

precedents.name: Dawn of War / Grey Goo — transformative unit upgrades
precedents.whatTheyDid: Upgrades that re-role a unit: Grey Goo's railgun turns single-target into AoE; Dawn of War's Mark of Khorne vs Mark of Tzeentch fundamentally change a squad's job (and are mutually exclusive).
precedents.outcome: Held up as exemplary upgrade design — dramatic, readable, immediately visible on the battlefield, and a real fork rather than a number bump.
precedents.lessonForUs: The gold standard for Layer 3 content. Frame contemporary upgrades the same way: 'drone swarm vs hypersonic vs laser-defense vs cyber' should change what a unit DOES, visibly, and lock out the alternative.

precedents.name: Sins of a Solar Empire — meta research trees
precedents.whatTheyDid: Separate research-screen trees (Logistics/Defense/Commerce/Mining/Research/Surveying + military) mixing flat bonuses with flavorful capstone abilities; each faction emphasizes different branches.
precedents.outcome: Good for long 4X-paced strategy and faction flavor, but the screen is large and the pacing is slow — closer to the grand-strategy feel the user explicitly wants to avoid.
precedents.lessonForUs: Cautionary on PACING and SCREEN SIZE. Borrow the idea of distinct branches as faction emphasis, but do NOT borrow the big always-open research panel — that's the Stellaris-slowness trap. Keep choices few, timed, and battlefield-facing.

research-eras.detail:
## The core design: three layers, not one tree

The user wants Civ-like possibility-space WITHOUT grand-strategy slowness. The way to get both is to split "research" into three layers that each do one job and each have a hard cap on how many choices are live at once.

### Layer 1 — ERAS (shared vertical spine; the AoE/RoN age model)
Four contemporary tiers, three advancement decisions:
- **Present Day** — precision artillery, MANPADS, 4th-gen MBTs, attack helos. The baseline RA-style loop.
- **Networked / EW Era** — recon drones, satellite/GPS ISR (reveal shroud), jamming, early cyber. Vision and information become weapons.
- **Autonomous Era** — drone SWARMS / loitering munitions (the real US "Replicator" thousands-of-cheap-drones concept), AI-assisted targeting, robotic ground units.
- **Near-Future** — hypersonics (Mach 5+ deep strike), directed-energy/laser point defense, layered missile defense, space/satellite supremacy.

Each advancement: researched at one HQ/R&D building, costs significant cash AND time during which that building produces nothing, and is gated behind a built structure (board commitment, RoN-style). Advancing RAISES THE CEILING (unlocks next units/buildings + next upgrade fork), it does NOT hand a flat buff. That preserves the teching-up-vs-spending-now gamble as the heartbeat of the system. Keep it to THREE advancements so the snowball/runaway-leader risk stays bounded.

### Layer 2 — DOCTRINE (one irreversible branching fork; the CoH model)
At game start (or first era-up) each player commits to ONE of: **Economy / Military / Defense / Diplomacy-Intel**. Irreversible for the match. Perks (3–5) unlock over time. This is:
- the answer to "econ/military/defense/diplomacy specialization paths,"
- the natural home for the user's "each country needs a unique troop + unique building" (a country's doctrine table IS its identity), and
- what makes diplomacy/EW/defense genuine strategic axes rather than garnish.
Show all four up front — it's the one big legible choice. Reveal the perks progressively as they unlock so the screen never floods.

### Layer 3 — ERA UPGRADES (few mutually-exclusive, readable forks; the Dawn of War / Universe at War model)
Per era, ~2–4 BIG forks that change HOW you fight, never a +1. Ground them in the counter-triangle of real tech:
- **Drone Swarm** (cheap massable loitering munitions) — beats massed armor.
- **Directed-Energy point defense** (laser turrets) — hard-counters the swarm.
- **Cyber / EW package** (jam enemy production/vision for a window) — beats anything networked.
- **Hypersonic strike** (one expensive deep-strike support power) — punishes turtling.
Constrain with "pick N of M" (Universe at War) so loadout = strategic statement. At most ONE fork open per production category at a time (progressive disclosure).

## The rules that keep it fast and legible
1. **No invisible tax.** If everyone always buys it in the same order, it's not a decision — fold it into the (free, automatic) era unlock or make it a fork. This is the single biggest lesson from the literature; StarCraft +1/+1 is the thing to avoid.
2. **Every choice is visible on the battlefield.** Qualitative, not quantitative (Grey Goo / Dawn of War standard).
3. **Tech competes with spend.** Research draws on the same cash (and ideally the same build slot/time) as units, so teching is never free background progress.
4. **~5 live choices max.** Era-up button + unlocked doctrine perks + the 1–2 open forks for what you're building. The full future tree lives in the read-only Codex, not the HUD.

## Engine fit (so this is buildable, not theoretical)
OpenRA already has the primitives: `ProvidesPrerequisite`, `TechTree`, `GrantConditionOnPrerequisite` + the condition system, and `SupportPower`/`SupportPowerManager`. Eras, doctrines, and upgrades become pure MiniYAML (prerequisite strings, conditions, support powers), validated by existing Lint rules at build time.

The ONE new piece needed: a player-actor trait, e.g. **`ResearchQueue`**, modeled directly on `ProductionQueue` (`OpenRA.Mods.Common/Traits/Player/ProductionQueue.cs`). It takes cost + time and, on completion, emits a prerequisite token / grants a condition. Everything downstream keys off that token exactly like building prerequisites do today. Keep it deterministic: integer cash, integer tick countdowns, `[Sync]` on state — no float/DateTime/Random in the tick path (the #1 desync class). Relevant existing files to model against: `OpenRA.Mods.Common/Traits/Player/ProductionQueue.cs`, `OpenRA.Mods.Common/Traits/Player/ProvidesPrerequisite.cs`, `OpenRA.Mods.Common/Traits/Player/TechTree.cs`, `OpenRA.Mods.Common/Traits/Conditions/GrantConditionOnPrerequisite.cs`, `OpenRA.Mods.Common/Traits/SupportPowers/SupportPower.cs`.

## Codex hook
Every era/doctrine/upgrade node carries a Codex entry (the existing Encyclopedia widget) describing the real ore/strategic resource or real military tech behind it. Strictly optional, asynchronous, never gates a decision — it's flavor and planning, not homework.

defense.executiveSummary:
The single most important real-world fact for your defense design is the cost-exchange ratio: modern defense is interesting precisely because it is an economic gamble, not a wall. A $35K Shahed drone can soak a $4.2M PAC-3 interceptor (a 120:1 loss for the defender), and Iran's actual doctrine is to launch cheap-drone waves to drain expensive interceptors, then send ballistic missiles when the defense is depleted (sources below). Translate THAT into the game and defense stops being "build wall, win" and becomes a live resource decision: which threats do I spend my expensive interceptors on, and where are my coverage gaps?

I recommend building modern defense as a LAYERED, TIERED, ACTIVE system with four pillars: (1) a tiered air-defense ladder — cheap gun SHORAD vs. mid Iron-Dome-style C-RAM vs. expensive Patriot/S-400 theater SAM — where each tier is cost-efficient only against its matching threat tier, so a smart attacker mismatches to bankrupt you; (2) interception as an explicit success-CHANCE mechanic (the engine already has chance-based missile deflection in JamsMissiles), with finite interceptor ammo so saturation is a real attack vector; (3) information/EW layer — early-warning radar, jammers, anti-drone RF, decoys, and counter-battery — that wins by denying targeting rather than killing, and is itself a fragile high-value target; (4) positional/fortification layer — bunkers, trenches, minefields, hardpoints — that shapes WHERE fights happen. Crucially, every defense must have an explicit, affordable counter, all of it must cost power/upkeep, and none of it should be mobile-with-the-army, so the failure mode (turtling into an unbreakable stalemate) is structurally prevented. The design north star: defense should buy you TIME and FORCE-ECONOMY, never invulnerability.
keyFindings: COST-EXCHANGE IS THE CORE FUN. Real modern defense is balanced on the knife-edge of cost: Iron Dome ($80K Tamir) beating a $300K rocket is a rare 0.27:1 WIN for the defender; a Patriot ($4.2M) vs a $35K drone is a catastrophic 120:1 LOSS. This asymmetry, not blast radius, is what makes layered defense a strategic puzzle. Model interceptors as consuming AMMO and COST per shot, so the player feels every intercept as a spend.

REAL DEFENSE IS A TIERED LADDER, NOT ONE TURRET. Modern IADS layers: VSHORAD/MANPADS (point, very low altitude) -> gun SHORAD + C-RAM like Iron Dome (rockets/artillery/cheap UAVs) -> medium/long SAM like Patriot PAC-3 / S-400 (aircraft, cruise missiles, area denial) -> high-altitude BMD like THAAD (ballistic terminal). Each tier is cost-efficient ONLY against its band; mismatching tiers (using THAAD on a drone) is how you go broke. This maps cleanly onto an RTS tech ladder of distinct defense buildings.

SATURATION DEFEATS ANY FIXED DEFENSE. Because interceptors are finite and expensive, the universal real-world counter is volume: cheap drone swarms exhaust the magazine, THEN the expensive missile leaks through. Israel had to build a cheap laser (Iron Beam) precisely because Tamir-vs-UAV economics were unsustainable. In-game this is the built-in anti-turtle valve: a defended base is beatable by out-producing its interceptor magazine.

ELECTRONIC WARFARE WINS BY DENIAL, NOT KILLS. 2024 battlefield reality: EW-enabled SEAD neutralizes radar networks without destroying every battery; GPS jamming/spoofing sends drones off-course; layered C-UAS stacks RF-detect + radar + optical + jammer + kinetic/laser. EW is a force-multiplier that degrades the ENEMY's targeting/accuracy and the player's own detection — a fundamentally different and more interesting verb than 'more DPS'. The engine already has JamsMissiles (chance-based) and DetectCloaked/jammer-circle rendering to build on.

TURTLING IS THE #1 FAILURE MODE AND IT IS A BALANCE PROBLEM, NOT A PLAYER PROBLEM. RTS design consensus: if defensive value-per-credit exceeds offensive value, both players sit and the game stalemates into a long drawn-out non-game. Turtles naturally accrue a stronger economy + leftover units + a better base. The fixes are structural: defenses must be strictly less cost-efficient than equivalent army value, immobile, power/upkeep-hungry, and counterable — and the map must reward EXPANDING (which a turtle can't defend everywhere).

TOWER-DEFENSE TEACHES POSITIONAL DEPTH: chokepoints concentrate firepower (favor AoE), target-priority micro (snipe the strongest/last) separates skilled play, and 'leak %' is a clean feedback signal. The transferable lesson: make defense about COVERAGE GEOMETRY and TARGET ALLOCATION, not raw stats. A defense line should have deliberate gaps the attacker probes and the defender patches — decisions, not autopilot.

THE ENGINE ALREADY SUPPORTS ~80% OF THIS. Confirmed hooks: JamsMissiles (chance-based missile deflection w/ relationship + range), DetectCloaked + RenderDetectionCircle/RenderJammerCircle, Mine/Minelayer, BlocksProjectiles, AmmoPool/ReloadAmmoPool (finite magazines), GrantExternalConditionWarhead + GrantExternalConditionPower (apply buffs/debuffs in an area), FirepowerMultiplier and friends (modifier stack), RevealsShroud/CreatesShroud (radar vs. gap), support-power framework, FireWarheads (area auras). Most new defenses are YAML compositions of existing traits; only a few (true point-defense interceptor, decoy, counter-battery) need modest new C# traits.
recommendations: BUILD THE AIR-DEFENSE LADDER AS 3 DISTINCT TIERS WITH BAND-LOCKED EFFICIENCY. Tier 1 'Gun SHORAD' (cheap, hitscan, unlimited ammo, only kills aircraft/drones/cheap rockets, useless vs. heavy missiles). Tier 2 'C-RAM / Iron-Dome' (medium cost, FINITE interceptor magazine via AmmoPool, chance-to-intercept rockets+artillery+missiles+drones — the workhorse). Tier 3 'Theater SAM' (Patriot/S-400 analog: expensive, long range, high single-shot chance, kills the heavy ballistic/cruise/superweapon-missile threats, but each interceptor COSTS credits and the magazine is tiny). Give each faction's tier-3 a flavor (US Patriot = best single-shot reliability; RU S-400 = longest range, wider area; Israel = cheapest interceptor cost). Tune so using a high tier on a low threat is a deliberate WASTE.

MAKE INTERCEPTION A SUCCESS-CHANCE + AMMO MECHANIC, NOT GUARANTEED. Reuse the JamsMissiles 'Chance' pattern but extend to a real PointDefense trait: each incoming projectile within range rolls against an intercept chance, consuming one round from an AmmoPool and (optionally) deducting a per-shot credit cost. Lower chance vs. faster/stealthier threats. This single mechanic creates the whole drama: probabilistic leaks, magazine depletion under saturation, and the economic sting of spending interceptors. Expose 'rounds remaining' as pips (engine already renders CargoPips/ammo pips) so the attacker can SEE a drained battery and exploit it. Determinism note: roll via the synced world RNG (MersenneTwister in world.Tick), never System.Random.

ADD AN INFORMATION/EW LAYER AS A SEPARATE, FRAGILE, HIGH-VALUE BUILDING CLASS. (a) Early-Warning Radar: extends RevealsShroud + grants nearby AD a to-hit/range bonus via GrantExternalConditionWarhead aura; kill it and the enemy's whole AD net degrades (real SEAD logic). (b) Jammer: area condition that REDUCES enemy weapon accuracy / disables enemy radar coverage (CreatesShroud-style) and lowers enemy missile homing — extend JamsMissiles. (c) Anti-Drone RF emitter: cheap, ONLY affects drone-class actors (a Targetable type), reflecting that RF C-UAS is the cost-efficient drone answer. (d) Counter-Battery Radar: on detecting an enemy artillery shot origin, auto-reveals + paints that shooter for your own arty/airstrike — turns enemy siege into a risk. Make all four soft (low HP) so they invite raids: information dominance is something you must DEFEND, creating attack/counter-attack tempo instead of turtling.

GIVE EVERY DEFENSE AN EXPLICIT, CHEAPER COUNTER AND PUBLISH IT IN THE CODEX. Saturation/swarm drains interceptor magazines; EW/jammers blind sensor nets; SEAD/anti-radiation strikes one-shot radars; artillery/siege outranges static turrets; engineers/infiltration disable or capture; EMP/power-grid attacks switch off the whole layer (defenses already inherit DisableOnLowPower). The Codex entry for each defense should NAME its counter and its real-world basis (e.g., 'Shahed swarm vs. Patriot — 120:1 cost ratio'). This teaches the meta-game and guarantees no defense is an autowin.

PRICE DEFENSE BELOW EQUIVALENT ARMY VALUE AND CHARGE POWER + UPKEEP. Hard anti-turtle rule from RTS design: a credit spent on static defense must buy strictly LESS combat value than the same credit in mobile units (defense's compensation is that it doesn't have to be microed and holds ground). Add ongoing power drain for radar/SAM/EW (engine supports negative Power and low-power disable), and consider an interceptor RESTOCK cost so a defense under constant pressure bleeds your economy. This makes 'how much defense' a real opportunity-cost decision and ensures the turtle is always poorer on the field.

FORCE COVERAGE-GAP DECISIONS WITH FINITE ARCS, RANGE RINGS, AND NO MOBILE PARITY. Render range/detection rings (RenderDetectionCircle/RenderRangeCircle exist) so players plan overlapping coverage and SEE the seams. Theater SAM should have a minimum range / dead zone (real Patriot can't engage point-blank), so it MUST be screened by SHORAD — layering becomes mandatory, not optional. Keep the strongest AD strictly immobile (building-only); allow only weak mobile SHORAD to travel with armies, so you can never deathball a perfect bubble around a moving attack. Coverage is a positional puzzle, not a stat check.

ADD POSITIONAL FORTIFICATION THAT SHAPES WHERE FIGHTS HAPPEN, NOT WALLS THAT END THEM. Bunkers/garrison points (engine has garrisonable Pillbox/Cargo): infantry inside get a defense bonus but can be flushed by flame/thermobaric/EMP. Trenches: a buildable terrain condition granting cover vs. small-arms but none vs. artillery — counter-able, positional. Minefields (Mine/Minelayer exist): cheap area-denial revealed/cleared by detectors and minesweepers — a tempo tax, not a wall. Hardpoints: empty emplacements you slot a weapon module into, letting one footprint flex between AA/AT/anti-infantry as the threat changes (decision under uncertainty). AVOID impassable mega-walls; favor things that slow, channel, and expose.

INTRODUCE DECOYS & CAMOUFLAGE AS A CHEAP MIND-GAME LAYER. Decoy emplacements (fake radar/SAM, like the existing FAKE buildings) bait expensive enemy SEAD/superweapons; camo-netting (Cloak trait) hides a real battery until it fires (first-shot reveal), rewarding ambush placement and punishing the attacker who guessed wrong. This adds bluffing and scouting value — the attacker must SPEND recon to know which battery is real — and is almost free to implement from existing FAKE/Cloak/Disguise traits.

ADD A GLOBAL SATURATION/SCRAMBLE TEMPO so defense stays ACTIVE. Interceptor magazines that take real time + credits to restock mean a defender must time when to 'go weapons-hot'; an EW 'jam burst' active ability (support-power framework) that briefly blinds an attacking wave but has cooldown; a counter-battery 'fire mission' the player triggers. The goal: the defender is making 2-4 live decisions during an assault (allocate interceptors, fire counter-battery, pop jammer, reposition mobile SHORAD), not watching turrets auto-fire. Active defense is the antidote to the passive-turtle non-game.

STRESS-TEST WITH THE EXPLICIT ANTI-STALEMATE CHECKLIST before shipping each defense: (1) Is there a counter that costs LESS than the defense? (2) Can a saturation/swarm attack drain or bypass it? (3) Does holding it cost ongoing economy (power/upkeep/restock)? (4) Is its strongest form immobile so it can't deathball? (5) Does expanding (which it can't cover everywhere) beat sitting behind it? If any answer is 'no', the defense is a turtle-enabler — re-tune. Pair this with map design that rewards taking ground (spread resources/objectives) so the dominant strategy is never 'sit'.
risks: TURTLE / STALEMATE (PRIMARY RISK): If defense is too cost-efficient the game degenerates into two players sitting behind impenetrable bubbles for 40 minutes — the exact non-game RTS designers warn about. Mitigation is structural and non-negotiable: defense priced below army value, immobile, power/upkeep-costly, saturation-vulnerable, and always counterable; map rewards expansion. Treat the anti-stalemate checklist as a gate, not a suggestion.

INTERCEPTION FEELS LIKE LUCK / FRUSTRATION: A pure random intercept roll can feel arbitrary ('my Patriot missed a nuke'). Mitigate with visible chance %, pity/streak smoothing if needed, clear telegraphing (which threats this tier can/can't beat), and by making chance a function of legible factors (tier match, EW state, range) the player controls — so leaks feel earned, not cheated.

DETERMINISM / DESYNC: Any chance-to-intercept, EW accuracy roll, or scatter MUST use the synced world RNG inside world.Tick and fixed-point math (no float/double/System.Random) — per the engine's determinism rules these are the #1 source of multiplayer desync. Every new trait reachable from the sim tick needs [Sync] discipline and the lint/yaml checks (make check) run before merge.

COMPLEXITY / COGNITIVE OVERLOAD: A full real-world IADS (4 tiers + EW + counter-battery + fortifications + decoys) can overwhelm players and bury the 'fast, engaging' goal under management. Mitigate by gating layers behind the tech tree (start simple, unlock depth), strong default auto-behaviors with optional manual override (target-priority toggles), clear range-ring/pip UI, and Codex onboarding. Per the user's vision: complexity should ENVELOP, not slow — introduce one layer at a time.

ART/SPRITE COST CEILING: Every new defense building and especially turreted/mobile SHORAD needs 2D sprites (and turrets need facings). The information/EW/decoy layer is the cheap win here — many entries are reskinned static structures or auras with minimal animation — so prioritize those for early prototyping and reserve expensive animated turret art for the tier-defining pieces.

FACTION BALANCE FRAGILITY: Tying defenses to real militaries (Patriot vs S-400 vs Iron Dome) invites both balance skew and political sensitivity. Differentiate by STRATEGIC ROLE (range vs. reliability vs. cost-per-shot vs. magazine size) rather than raw power, keep aggregate faction defense value equal, and frame Codex entries factually/educationally to stay neutral.

POWER-GRID SINGLE POINT OF FAILURE: If the whole AD/EW net depends on power and one EMP/power raid switches it all off, defense can swing from oppressive to useless in one move — exciting, but potentially a coin-flip. Mitigate with partial/graceful degradation, some battery-backed core defenses, and counterplay against the EMP itself.
defense.detail:
REAL-WORLD MODEL -> GAMEPLAY MAPPING (the four pillars)

PILLAR 1 — TIERED INTEGRATED AIR DEFENSE (the ladder)
Real IADS layers by altitude/threat band: VSHORAD/MANPADS -> gun-SHORAD + C-RAM (Iron Dome) -> medium/long SAM (Patriot PAC-3, S-400) -> high BMD (THAAD). Each tier is cost-efficient only in its band. Game translation = 3 buildable AD buildings on the tech tree:
- Gun SHORAD (T1, cheap, hitscan, infinite ammo): kills aircraft, drones, cheap rockets. Hopeless vs. heavy missiles. The flak-truck of the set; also the only AD allowed to be mobile (weak).
- C-RAM / Iron-Dome (T2, medium, FINITE magazine, chance-to-intercept): the workhorse vs. rockets, artillery shells, cruise missiles, drone swarms. AmmoPool depletes; restock costs time+credits.
- Theater SAM (T3, expensive, long range, minimum-range dead zone, tiny costly magazine): the only answer to ballistic/superweapon/heavy-cruise threats. Has a dead zone so it MUST be screened by T1/T2 — this is what forces real layering. Faction flavor: US Patriot = highest single-shot reliability; RU S-400 = longest range + widest coverage; IL Iron-Dome line = cheapest interceptor cost (best economy).

PILLAR 2 — INTERCEPTION AS SUCCESS-CHANCE + FINITE AMMO (the core mechanic)
This is the heart of "cool, strategic defense." Real cost-exchange: Iron Dome $80K Tamir vs $300K rocket = 0.27:1 (defender wins); Patriot $4.2M vs $35K Shahed = 120:1 (defender loses badly). Iran's doctrine: swarm cheap drones to drain interceptors, then send the ballistic missile. Game mechanic:
- New PointDefense trait (extend the existing JamsMissiles chance model): each incoming projectile in range rolls intercept chance, consumes 1 AmmoPool round, optionally deducts per-shot credits.
- Lower chance vs. faster/stealthier/saturating threats; chance modified by EW state and tier-match.
- Magazine depletion is VISIBLE (ammo pips). A drained battery is a real, exploitable opening. Restock = time + money.
This single system produces: probabilistic leaks (tension), saturation as a real attack (anti-turtle valve), and economic pain per intercept (defense isn't free). Determinism: roll on synced world RNG, fixed-point only.

PILLAR 3 — INFORMATION / ELECTRONIC WARFARE (win by denial, not kills)
2024 reality: EW-SEAD blinds radar nets without killing every battery; GPS jam/spoof sends drones off-course; layered C-UAS = RF-detect + radar + optical + jammer + kinetic/laser. Four soft, high-value buildings:
- Early-Warning Radar: extends shroud reveal + grants an accuracy/range buff aura to nearby AD (GrantExternalConditionWarhead). Kill it (SEAD) and the whole AD net degrades. Soft HP -> invites raids.
- Jammer: area condition reducing enemy weapon accuracy + missile homing + radar coverage (extend JamsMissiles + CreatesShroud). 
- Anti-Drone RF: cheap, affects ONLY drone-class Targetables — the cost-efficient drone answer, mirroring real C-UAS economics.
- Counter-Battery Radar: detects enemy artillery shot origin, reveals+paints the shooter for your own arty/airstrike. Makes enemy siege risky; a defensive building that enables OFFENSE.
Because these are fragile and decisive, information dominance becomes something you attack and defend — generating tempo instead of turtling.

PILLAR 4 — POSITIONAL FORTIFICATION (shape where fights happen)
- Bunkers/garrison (engine: garrisonable pillbox/cargo): infantry inside get a bonus; flushed by flame/thermobaric/EMP.
- Trenches: buildable terrain condition, cover vs. small-arms, none vs. artillery — positional, counterable.
- Minefields (engine: Mine/Minelayer): cheap area-denial, cleared by detectors/minesweepers — a tempo tax, not a wall.
- Hardpoints: empty emplacements you slot AA/AT/anti-infantry modules into; flex the footprint as the threat shifts (decision under uncertainty).
- Decoys & camo (engine: FAKE buildings + Cloak/Disguise): fake batteries bait enemy SEAD/superweapons; camo-netting hides a real battery until first shot. Adds bluffing + scouting value.
AVOID impassable mega-walls. Favor slow/channel/expose.

ANTI-TURTLE DESIGN (the load-bearing constraint)
RTS consensus: if defensive value-per-credit > offensive, games stalemate into long non-games; turtles also accrue better economy + leftover units + better base. Structural fixes, enforced as a pre-ship checklist per defense: (1) priced below equivalent army value; (2) saturation/swarm can drain or bypass it; (3) costs ongoing power/upkeep/restock; (4) strongest form is immobile (no deathball bubble); (5) expanding beats sitting (spread map resources/objectives so a turtle can't cover everywhere). Active-defense layer keeps the defender making 2-4 live decisions per assault (allocate interceptors, fire counter-battery, pop jam burst, reposition mobile SHORAD) — defense as verbs, not autopilot.

TOWER-DEFENSE LESSONS APPLIED
Chokepoints concentrate firepower (favor AoE placement); target-priority micro (snipe strongest/last) separates skilled play -> expose target-priority toggles on AD; "leak %" is clean feedback -> surface interception/leak stats. Core transferable idea: defense is about COVERAGE GEOMETRY + TARGET ALLOCATION, not raw stats. Range rings + dead zones make seams visible and patchable.

ENGINE IMPLEMENTATION NOTES (what exists vs. what's new)
Already present (YAML-composable): JamsMissiles (chance + relationship + range), DetectCloaked + RenderDetectionCircle/RenderJammerCircle, Mine/Minelayer, BlocksProjectiles, AmmoPool/ReloadAmmoPool (finite magazines + pips), GrantExternalConditionWarhead + GrantExternalConditionPower (area buffs/debuffs), FirepowerMultiplier/DetectCloakedMultiplier (modifier stack), RevealsShroud/CreatesShroud (radar vs gap), DisableOnLowPower (EMP/power-raid hook), FAKE buildings, Cloak/Disguise, support-power framework, FireWarheads (area auras).
Modest new C# traits needed: (1) PointDefense (per-projectile intercept roll consuming AmmoPool + optional credit cost) — model on JamsMissiles; (2) CounterBattery (detect shot origin -> reveal/paint shooter); (3) Hardpoint module-swap (or approximate with build-on-build / upgrades). Everything routed through world.Tick must use synced RNG + fixed-point (WDist/WAngle), [Sync] fields, and pass make check / lint before merge.

Relevant repo files for the implementing team (all absolute):
- /Users/ashishnaik/Projects/openra/OpenRA.Mods.Common/Traits/JamsMissiles.cs (chance-based deflection — template for PointDefense)
- /Users/ashishnaik/Projects/openra/OpenRA.Mods.Common/Traits/AmmoPool.cs and ReloadAmmoPool.cs (finite interceptor magazines + restock)
- /Users/ashishnaik/Projects/openra/OpenRA.Mods.Common/Traits/DetectCloaked.cs + Render/RenderDetectionCircle.cs / RenderJammerCircle (sensor + ring UI)
- /Users/ashishnaik/Projects/openra/OpenRA.Mods.Common/Warheads/GrantExternalConditionWarhead.cs + SupportPowers/GrantExternalConditionPower.cs (EW auras / active jam burst)
- /Users/ashishnaik/Projects/openra/OpenRA.Mods.Common/Traits/Mine.cs + Minelayer.cs (minefields), BlocksProjectiles.cs (hard cover)
- /Users/ashishnaik/Projects/openra/mods/ra/rules/structures.yaml (existing AGUN/SAM/PBOX/HBOX/IRON/GAP patterns to extend) and defaults.yaml (^Defense / ^AutoTargetAir templates)

SUGGESTED MINIMUM-VIABLE PROTOTYPE (cheap-art-first): ship the EW/information + interception layer first (mostly auras, reskinned statics, and the PointDefense trait) before investing in expensive animated turret/SHORAD sprite sets. That validates the "active, economic, counterable defense" fantasy at the lowest art cost.

SOURCES: CSIS 'Cost and Value in Air and Missile Defense Intercepts' (https://www.csis.org/analysis/cost-and-value-air-and-missile-defense-intercepts); Modern War Institute 'The Indispensable Interceptor' (https://mwi.westpoint.edu/the-indispensable-interceptor-air-defense-and-the-problem-of-cost-exchange-logic/); MissileStrikes cost-exchange analysis (https://missilestrikes.com/cost-analysis/) and EW guide (https://missilestrikes.com/guide/what-is-electronic-warfare/); Norsk Luftvern air-defense comparison matrix (https://norskluftvern.com/2026/01/03/the-complete-air-defense-systems-comparison-matrix-western-systems-ranked-and-analyzed/); Wikipedia 'Comparison of anti-ballistic missile systems' (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Comparison_of_anti-ballistic_missile_systems); drone-warfare.com C-UAS EW (https://drone-warfare.com/counter-uas/electronic-warfare/); RTS turtle/stalemate design (https://medium.com/how-to-be-good-at-real-time-strategy-games/how-to-be-good-at-real-time-strategy-games-pt-1-41012b02eb52 and https://gamedev.net/forums/topic/281520-rts-game-duration-and-repetition/); tower-defense design (https://www.designthegame.com/learning/tutorial/tower-defense-design-guide and https://www.stardock.com/games/article/495008/siege-of-centauri-dev-journal-what-makes-a-good-tower-defense-game).
