The system reports interception probability and only engages threats predicted to hit defended areas.
precedents.outcome: The only widely-cited case where the defender's cost-per-intercept actually beats the threat (~0.27:1 vs cheap rockets), but still forced to add a cheaper tier for the drone band.
precedents.lessonForUs: Model interception as a finite, costed, probabilistic resource and give each threat band a cost-efficient matching defender. The need for a cheaper anti-drone tier (laser/RF) is the in-game justification for a low-cost SHORAD/anti-drone layer and is the structural answer to swarm saturation.

precedents.name: Shahed-drone saturation doctrine (Iran)
precedents.whatTheyDid: Mixes cheap $35K Shahed-136 drones with expensive ballistic missiles, launching drone waves first to exhaust expensive interceptors (PAC-3 at $4.2M), then sending ballistic missiles through the depleted defense.
precedents.outcome: Forces a 120:1 adverse cost-exchange on the defender; degrades even top-tier AD by magazine depletion rather than by defeating any single interceptor.
precedents.lessonForUs: This is the built-in anti-turtle mechanic: finite interceptor magazines + saturation means any fixed defense is beatable by out-producing its magazine. Make magazines visible and restock costly so 'drain then punch through' is a real, readable strategy.

precedents.name: C&C: Generals — linked defensive structures + faction defense identity
precedents.whatTheyDid: Gave each faction distinct defensive identities (US high-tech linked defenses that share targeting/data; others cheaper/spammier), with base structures split into production / support / defensive counter-measures, and emphasized unit-mix counters over static walls.
precedents.outcome: Defenses felt faction-flavored and required combined-arms to crack, but Generals also showed superweapon spam and base-crawl can dominate if economy/defense aren't checked.
precedents.lessonForUs: Differentiate factions by defensive ROLE (linked sensor net vs cheap mass vs elite interceptors), not raw power, mirroring real Patriot/S-400/Iron-Dome distinctions — and watch the superweapon/base-crawl failure mode.

precedents.name: Iron Dome / IADS minimum-range + altitude layering (Patriot dead zone)
precedents.whatTheyDid: Real theater SAMs (Patriot) have a minimum engagement range and altitude band, so they cannot defend themselves at point-blank and must be screened by short-range systems; the architecture is explicitly layered by altitude.
precedents.outcome: Layering is mandatory in reality — no single tier is self-sufficient; SEAD against the radar collapses the whole net.
precedents.lessonForUs: Give the top-tier SAM a dead zone so it REQUIRES SHORAD screening, making layered placement a forced positional puzzle rather than a single super-turret, and make the radar a fragile linchpin (SEAD target) to create attack/counter tempo.

precedents.name: Tower-defense genre (chokepoint + target-priority + leak design)
precedents.whatTheyDid: Built engagement on coverage geometry (chokepoints concentrate AoE), real-time target-priority micro (snipe strongest/last), escalating waves, and 'leak %' as a difficulty/feedback signal.
precedents.outcome: A durable, addictive loop of anticipation -> adjustment; skilled play separated from casual by allocation/positioning decisions rather than stats.
precedents.lessonForUs: Make RTS defense about COVERAGE GAPS and TARGET ALLOCATION (range rings, dead zones, priority toggles, leak feedback) so it stays an active decision, and lean on chokepoints/positioning instead of raw turret HP — directly counters the passive-turtle problem.

countries.executiveSummary: A 12-faction asymmetric roster for a "Contemporary" total-conversion of OpenRA, designed to slot directly onto the engine's proven sub-faction template (each faction = a distinct PLAYSTYLE expressed through one signature UNIT + one signature BUILDING + a STRATEGIC NICHE), not power tiers. The design goal is real-military-doctrine flavor translated into the five OpenRA loops (economy, production/tech, rock-paper-scissors combat, support powers, veterancy), with the requested Civilization/Stellaris "possibility space" delivered through a lightweight research/diplomacy/codex layer rather than slow grand-strategy. Each country is grounded in its actual force structure: USA = networked air/naval power-projection; China = mass + A2/AD missile umbrella + drones; Russia = armor + EW + massed artillery; Germany = engineering/armor durability; France = expeditionary precision + nuclear deterrent; UK = naval/expeditionary/intel; Israel = active-protection + interception + precision intel; India = layered mixed arsenal + numbers + indigenization; Japan = naval/Aegis missile-defense + robotics; South Korea = sensor-to-shooter C4I + artillery + drones; Turkey = cheap attritable drones + land-air integration; Iran = asymmetric swarm + cheap mass + denial. Balance is achieved by giving every faction a clear strength AND a clear exploitable weakness, and by ensuring each unique unit obeys strict strong-vs/weak-vs counters so no faction is universally dominant. Recommendation on naming: use LIGHTLY-FICTIONALIZED bloc/archetype names with real-world flavor (see sensitivityNotes), NOT raw national branding, to stay respectful and avoid implying endorsement of any state or current conflict.
countries.balancingPhilosophy: Asymmetric-but-fair is enforced by four rules borrowed from the existing OpenRA DNA. (1) EVERY faction has a paired strength+weakness: the thing that makes it strong is also the seam an opponent attacks (e.g. USA's networked buff collapses if its command building dies; Iran's cheap swarm folds to splash/area weapons; Germany's armor is slow and air-vulnerable). No faction is good at everything — armies remain compositions. (2) Signature units are SIDEGRADES with hard counters, never stat-superior versions of a common unit. Each unique unit ships an explicit strong-vs / weak-vs so the rock-paper-scissors read stays legible (the engine already encodes this via armor types + Warhead modifiers). (3) Power budget parity: a "strong" signature unit costs more, is build-limited, or has a fragile enabler building; a "cheap/mass" faction trades durability and tech ceiling for numbers. Cost, build-limit, and prerequisite gating are the balance dials, exactly as Tanya (max 1) and the Mammoth (slow apex) already work. (4) Each faction's signature BUILDING is an ENABLER, not a flat economy boost — it changes HOW you play (a forward command node, an interception dome, a market/diplomacy hub), so picking a faction is picking a strategy, not a tier. The strategic-depth ask (Civ/Stellaris envelope) is delivered cheaply: a small RESEARCH tree (3-4 mutually-exclusive doctrine picks per faction, reusing the existing prerequisite system), DIPLOMACY stances (already in-engine) with a trade/market building, and a CODEX (the existing Encyclopedia widget) that teaches counters and real-world ore/strategic-resource lore — adding decisions without slowing the real-time pace. Art cost is the true ceiling (32-facing sprites per unit), so the roster is deliberately scoped to ONE new signature unit per faction sharing a common modern-military base set; everything else (buildings, powers, research, codex) is rules/YAML/script-cheap.

roster.country: United States (bloc archetype: 'The Federation' / networked power-projection superpower)
roster.militaryIdentity: Air and naval power-projection backed by stealth and a battlefield-wide data network (JADC2-style 'decouple sensors from shooters'). Doctrine: see first, connect everything, let any platform fire on any target. Carriers, F-35 stealth, networked precision.
roster.signatureUnitRealBasis: F-35 Lightning II / F-22 stealth fighter, multi-domain networked strike
roster.signatureUnitRole: Cloaked-until-firing air superiority + precision ground strike that also acts as a mobile sensor, revealing fog and feeding the network. Strong vs: ground armor clusters, undefended production, and any faction relying on massed slow units. Weak vs: dedicated SAM/air-defense buildings and air-defense units (Russia/China/Japan domes), and cheap massed AA that out-trades its high cost.
roster.signatureBuildingRealBasis: JADC2 / Combined Joint All-Domain Command & Control battle-management node
roster.signatureBuildingEffect: While alive, grants a passive 'networked' aura: all friendly units within vision share targeting — bonus accuracy/range and the ability to fire on targets spotted by ANY allied unit (sensor-shooter decoupling). High-value and fragile: destroying it strips the whole army's buff, creating a clear counter-play target.
roster.strategicNiche: Tempo and information dominance. Wins by scouting, picking fights it has already 'seen', and surgical air strikes — but is expensive per unit and collapses if its command node is sniped or its air is denied. The 'finesse/precision' anchor of the roster (RA-Allies energy, modernized).

roster.country: China (bloc archetype: 'The Continental Bloc' / mass + missile-umbrella + drones)
roster.militaryIdentity: Anti-access/area-denial: a dense missile umbrella that makes enemy ships/aircraft pay to enter, combined with industrial mass production and growing drone fleets. Quantity + a defensive 'bubble'.
roster.signatureUnitRealBasis: DF-21D / DF-26 'carrier-killer' anti-ship/area ballistic missile (mobile TEL)
roster.signatureUnitRole: Long-range, slow-firing mobile launcher that creates a no-go zone: devastating vs large/expensive targets (capital ships, superheavy units, structures) inside its huge range. Strong vs: high-cost 'big' units and naval/air assets that stray into range; punishes power-projection factions (USA/UK/Japan). Weak vs: cheap fast swarms that close the distance, and its own fragility/slow reload — it dies fast to raids and has minimal self-defense.
roster.signatureBuildingRealBasis: Layered IADS networking radar + SAM + coastal missile batteries
roster.signatureBuildingEffect: Projects a large defensive 'denial dome' around the base: enemy aircraft and missiles inside take accuracy penalties and reduced speed, and friendly long-range batteries gain extended range. Turns the home theater into contested space — but the dome is stationary, so it rewards turtling and is vulnerable on the offense.
roster.strategicNiche: Zone control and attrition-by-denial. Excels at holding ground and making the enemy bleed to approach; mass-produces cheap units to flood objectives. Weak when forced to attack OUT of its bubble onto open ground. The 'control + mass' anchor.

roster.country: Russia (bloc archetype: 'The Northern Union' / armor + EW + artillery)
roster.militaryIdentity: Heavy mechanized armor spearheads supported by massed artillery and pervasive electronic warfare (the 'reconnaissance-fire' idea: jam the enemy's coordination, then crush with steel and tube/rocket fire).
roster.signatureUnitRealBasis: T-14 Armata universal platform (designed for EW/recon/air-defense designation roles, signature-reduction)
roster.signatureUnitRole: A durable heavy tank that doubles as a mobile jammer: suppresses enemy targeting (reduces accuracy/range of nearby foes) and shrugs off precision strikes via signature reduction. Strong vs: networked/precision factions (USA/Israel/Korea) whose edge is coordination — the jam blunts them; and vs infantry/light vehicles head-on. Weak vs: massed cheap units that overwhelm by numbers, dedicated tank-hunter aircraft/ATGM units, and flanking (slow, expensive, few of them).
roster.signatureBuildingEffect: Unlocks and coordinates a saturation barrage support power and gives all friendly artillery a 'time-on-target' bonus (tighter, harder-hitting volleys) when firing on a spotted target. Rewards a scout-then-shell playstyle; the barrage is telegraphed (a beacon), per OpenRA support-power convention, so it breaks sieges but can be dodged.
roster.strategicNiche: Brute attrition with a tech twist: degrade the enemy's coordination via EW, then win the slugfest with armor and artillery. Strong in set-piece pushes, weak to mobility and swarms. The 'overpower/heavy' anchor (RA-Soviet energy, modernized).

roster.country: Germany (bloc archetype: 'The Rhine Compact' / engineering + armor durability)
roster.militaryIdentity: Engineering excellence and armored survivability — the Leopard tradition: superbly built, durable, well-protected platforms and combat-engineering/logistics mastery. Quality over quantity, reliability, repair.
roster.signatureUnitRole: The most durable frontline tank in the game with superior frontal armor and self-field-repair when stationary; an anchor that holds a line. Strong vs: other armor in a straight fight and sustained frontal engagements (out-survives trades). Weak vs: top-attack/air (drones, strike aircraft), flanking and rear shots, and missile-denial factions; it is slow and expensive, so it can be bypassed or kited.
roster.signatureBuildingRealBasis: Bundeswehr combat-engineering / armored recovery & logistics doctrine
roster.signatureBuildingEffect: Auto-repairs nearby vehicles faster, enables a deployable forward repair/rearm pad and rapid pontoon/bridge & defensive-emplacement construction (terraforming/fortify). Lets Germany project a durable, self-sustaining front line and convert map terrain into defensible ground.
roster.strategicNiche: Resilient positional warfare and force preservation (synergizes with veterancy — its tanks survive to become aces). Wins long games of held ground and repaired armor; loses to mobility, air, and being out-tempo'd. The 'durability/engineering' anchor.

roster.country: France (bloc archetype: 'The Gallic Republic' / expeditionary precision + deterrent)
roster.militaryIdentity: Independent expeditionary force with strategic autonomy: rapid-reaction precision strike (Rafale), versatile do-everything platforms, and a credible last-resort deterrent. Self-reliant, flexible, prestige-tech.
roster.signatureUnitRole: A flexible multirole aircraft that swaps loadouts (anti-air / anti-ground / anti-ship) on the fly, enabling fast expeditionary raids anywhere on the map. Strong vs: factions that over-commit to one domain (it adapts to counter them) and undefended expansions. Weak vs: dedicated specialists in their own lane (a pure air-superiority fighter or a pure SAM out-trades it 1v1) and concentrated air defense; jack-of-all-trades, master of none.
roster.signatureBuildingRealBasis: Force de dissuasion — independent nuclear/strategic deterrent (handled as a defensive deterrent, not a city-buster — see sensitivityNotes)
roster.signatureBuildingEffect: A telegraphed last-resort support power AND a passive deterrence aura: while the silo stands, enemy superweapon/support-power charge rates are slowed in retaliation (mutual-deterrence flavor). Encourages a stand-off, autonomy-focused game rather than spamming a doomsday button.
roster.strategicNiche: Adaptable independence and stand-off pressure: never the strongest in any single domain, but never helpless in any either; the deterrent discourages enemy super-power spam. Rewards a flexible, reactive commander. The 'versatility/autonomy' anchor.

roster.country: United Kingdom (bloc archetype: 'The Isles Coalition' / naval-expeditionary + intel)
roster.militaryIdentity: Expeditionary naval power and signals/intelligence tradition: carrier-enabled reach, special-forces precision, and superior reconnaissance/early-warning. Punches above its weight via information and the sea.
roster.signatureUnitRealBasis: UK Special Air Service / special-reconnaissance + signals intelligence
roster.signatureUnitRole: Elite cloaked infantry that infiltrates, designates targets for precision fire, sabotages structures, and provides deep vision. Strong vs: economy/tech targets, undefended backlines, and information-poor opponents (devastating raids and intel). Weak vs: detector units/buildings (loses cloak and dies fast), and any direct stand-up fight — extremely fragile, a scalpel not a hammer.
roster.signatureBuildingRealBasis: Royal Navy carrier-strike command + GCHQ-style early-warning/SIGINT
roster.signatureBuildingEffect: Reveals enemy support-power launches and incoming attacks early (radar/early-warning), periodically pings enemy unit locations (intel sweep), and enables off-map naval/carrier strike support powers. Turns information into the win condition.
roster.strategicNiche: Intelligence asymmetry and expeditionary raiding: wins by always knowing more and hitting where the enemy isn't. Thin if forced into attrition or if its intel building is destroyed. Pairs naturally as the naval/recon counterpart to the USA's networked air. The 'information/raiding' anchor.

roster.country: Israel (bloc archetype: 'The Levant Shield' / active-protection + interception + precision)
roster.militaryIdentity: Survive-everything defensive tech plus precision intel-driven strikes: active protection on every vehicle (Trophy), rocket/missile interception (Iron Dome), and intelligence that finds the target before anyone else.
roster.signatureUnitRealBasis: Merkava Mk4 with Trophy active protection system (APS)
roster.signatureUnitRole: A medium tank with a hard-kill APS that intercepts the FIRST incoming missile/rocket each few seconds, then returns fire — extremely strong vs missile/rocket/ATGM and drone factions (Turkey/Iran/China/India). Strong vs: anything that relies on guided projectiles and alpha-strike missiles. Weak vs: gun/kinetic and beam weapons (APS can't stop shells), and saturation — multiple simultaneous missiles overwhelm the interceptor. Mid armor otherwise.
roster.signatureBuildingRealBasis: Iron Dome short-range rocket/artillery interception system
roster.signatureBuildingEffect: Stationary defensive structure that auto-intercepts a limited number of incoming enemy projectiles per interval (artillery shells, rockets, missiles, super-power munitions) over an area — but has finite interceptors that recharge, so saturation can punch through. Hard-counters artillery/missile/super-weapon factions; useless against ground assault.
roster.strategicNiche: Defensive denial of enemy precision: neutralizes the very missile/drone/artillery strengths other factions are built around, forcing them into kinetic ground fights Israel can win with intel and positioning. Weak to massed kinetic armor and saturation. The 'counter-the-counter / interception' anchor.

roster.country: India (bloc archetype: 'The Subcontinent Federation' / layered mixed arsenal + numbers)
roster.militaryIdentity: A pragmatic, layered mixed arsenal: imported + indigenous systems side by side, a supersonic cruise-missile punch (BrahMos) behind a multi-layer air-defense shield (S-400/Akash), backed by sheer numbers and mass mobilization.
roster.signatureUnitRealBasis: BrahMos supersonic cruise missile (mobile launcher, Mach 2.8 precision)
roster.signatureUnitRole: A fast, hard-hitting precision missile launcher that strikes high-value targets at long range with little warning (supersonic = short reaction window). Strong vs: key structures, command nodes, and superheavy units (a surgical 'delete the enemy's enabler building' tool). Weak vs: interception/active-protection (Israel, Japan, China domes catch it) and fast harassment — it's expensive, fragile, and slow-firing, needing the air-defense shield to survive.
roster.signatureBuildingRealBasis: S-400 + indigenous Akash multi-layer integrated air defense
roster.signatureBuildingEffect: Creates a tiered anti-air/anti-missile umbrella (long+short range) protecting the base AND, crucially, the BrahMos launchers under it — survivability for the offensive arm. Also allows cheap mass-infantry/militia call-ups (numbers doctrine) via a mobilization power.
roster.strategicNiche: Shielded long-range punch plus expendable numbers: hides a fragile precision strike behind a deep defensive shield, then snipes the enemy's key assets while a numerous cheap army holds the field. Weak if the shield is saturated or out-maneuvered. The 'protected-strike + numbers' anchor.

roster.country: Japan (bloc archetype: 'The Eastern Maritime Pact' / naval Aegis defense + robotics)
roster.militaryIdentity: Constitutionally defensive but technologically elite: world-class Aegis missile-defense destroyers, sea-lane protection, and leading robotics/unmanned systems. Defensive posture, exquisite tech, reactive precision.
roster.signatureUnitRealBasis: Maya/Kongō-class Aegis BMD destroyer (+ Izumo-class F-35B influence)
roster.signatureUnitRole: A premium warship that shoots down enemy aircraft, missiles AND ballistic/super-power projectiles across a wide radius — a mobile shield for the fleet/army. Strong vs: air, missile, and superweapon factions (protects allies from the sky). Weak vs: massed surface/ground assault and submarines/cheap swarm boats (it's an anti-air/anti-missile specialist, poor at brawling), and it is very expensive.
roster.signatureBuildingRealBasis: Japanese defense robotics / unmanned ground & sea systems R&D
roster.signatureBuildingEffect: Periodically deploys free autonomous drone/robot escorts (unmanned ground vehicles, sentry drones) and lets damaged vehicles be remotely operated when crews would die (units fight on at reduced effectiveness instead of dying once). Force-multiplies a small, high-tech, defensive army.
roster.strategicNiche: Defensive tech-superiority and attrition denial from the sea: a small elite force that shields itself and allies from air/missile threats and replaces losses with robots. Strong reactively; weak when forced to assault or out-massed on land. The 'defensive high-tech / naval shield' anchor.

roster.country: South Korea (bloc archetype: 'The Peninsula Republic' / C4I sensor-to-shooter + artillery)
roster.militaryIdentity: Networked, sensor-to-shooter artillery state: every platform (K2 tank, K9 howitzer, K239 MLRS) is born to share data and shorten the kill chain. Drones spot, the network decides, fires land in seconds. Tech + tubes + speed-of-decision.
roster.signatureUnitRealBasis: K9 Thunder 155mm self-propelled howitzer + drone spotting / counter-battery
roster.signatureUnitRole: Mobile artillery that fires faster and more accurately when a friendly scout/drone has spotted the target, and auto-counter-fires at enemy artillery (counter-battery). Strong vs: static defenses, clustered units, and other artillery (wins the counter-battery duel). Weak vs: fast units that close inside its minimum range, air, and being un-spotted (much weaker without a scout feeding it) — fragile up close.
roster.signatureBuildingEffect: Dramatically shortens the 'kill chain': any target spotted by any friendly unit/drone is instantly shared, and friendly artillery/missiles within range get a rapid first-strike bonus on newly-spotted targets. Also boosts drone/scout production. The whole army fires faster the more it sees.
roster.strategicNiche: Speed-of-the-kill-chain: out-scouts and out-shoots from range before the enemy can react, dominating with artillery the instant it has vision. Collapses if blinded (scouts killed) or rushed into close combat. A faster, more offensive cousin to USA's network — artillery-flavored. The 'sensor-to-shooter tempo' anchor.

roster.country: Turkey (bloc archetype: 'The Anatolian Alliance' / cheap attritable drones + land-air)
roster.militaryIdentity: Pioneer of cheap, mass, attritable armed drones tightly integrated with ground fire and electronic warfare (the TB2 'new method of war'): swarms of affordable UCAVs that spot, strike, and are expendable.
roster.signatureUnitRole: Cheap, mass-producible armed drone that loiters, scouts, and precision-strikes ground targets; you field MANY. Strong vs: unsupported armor and artillery (death-by-a-thousand-cuts, and it spots for your own guns), and economy harassment. Weak vs: any anti-air (dedicated AA units, SAM buildings, Israel/Japan/China domes shred them), and EW jamming; individually flimsy, only strong in numbers and only vs the unprepared.
roster.signatureBuildingRealBasis: Turkish UCAV ground-control + KORAL electronic-warfare integration
roster.signatureBuildingEffect: Cheapens and speeds drone production, extends drone loiter range/vision across the map, and projects an EW jamming field that degrades enemy air-defense accuracy — opening windows for the drone swarm. Makes drones the cheap backbone of the whole army.
roster.strategicNiche: Cheap attritable air harassment + spotting: floods the map with expendable eyes and small strikes, integrating air and ground fire — but is hard-countered by any opponent that invests in air defense, forcing a constant tech race. The 'cheap drone-swarm + EW' anchor (distinct from Iran by being precision/air-focused, not mass-ground).

roster.country: Iran (bloc archetype: 'The Persian Resistance' / asymmetric swarm + denial)
roster.militaryIdentity: Asymmetric attrition and saturation: cheap suicide drones (Shahed), swarms of fast attack craft, mines and decentralized 'mosaic defense' designed to deplete a richer enemy's expensive interceptors and deny key terrain. Cheap mass vs costly precision.
roster.signatureUnitRealBasis: Shahed-136 loitering munition (cheap one-way attack drone, fielded in swarms)
roster.signatureUnitRole: Dirt-cheap one-shot loitering munition built in large salvos; overwhelms by saturation, trading favorably against expensive interceptors/structures. Strong vs: high-value/expensive targets and interception-based factions (forces them to 'waste' costly defenses on cheap drones — economic asymmetry). Weak vs: cheap area/splash anti-air and flak that kills many per shot, and good early detection; each drone is trivially killed — the threat is only the swarm's mass.
roster.signatureBuildingRealBasis: IRGC decentralized 'mosaic defense' + fast-attack-craft / asymmetric production
roster.signatureBuildingEffect: Cheap, fast-to-build, redundant production node (you build many small ones instead of one big factory) so the faction is hard to decapitate — losing buildings barely slows you. Continuously spawns cheap militia/fast-boats/drones and lets units hide/ambush. Resilience and mass over quality.
roster.strategicNiche: Cost-imposition and saturation: never wins a quality fight, wins by being un-killable as a system and forcing the enemy to spend $10 to stop $1. Strong vs rich precision factions; weak vs cheap area-effect weapons and patient, well-defended opponents. The 'asymmetric swarm/denial' anchor — the deliberate mirror to the USA superpower at the opposite end of the cost/quality axis.

countries.sensitivityNotes: RECOMMENDATION: use lightly-fictionalized bloc/archetype names with clearly real-world-inspired flavor, NOT raw national branding or flags. Concretely: keep recognizable visual/doctrinal DNA (a 'Northern Union' that is obviously Russia-flavored, a 'Levant Shield' obviously Israel-flavored) but rename factions, units and buildings to fictional callsigns ('Specter', 'Bayrak UCAV', 'Aril') rather than literal designations. Why: (1) it sidesteps implying the developers endorse, rank, or take sides between real states or in any live conflict; (2) it gives design freedom to balance without 'but the real X is stronger' arguments; (3) it follows OpenRA/Red Alert's own established 'lightly-fictionalized real powers' tradition, so it feels native to the engine. Additional guardrails: (a) Frame ALL factions as defensive/archetypal 'doctrines', not aggressors — no faction's lore should reference real wars, occupations, or specific adversaries; pair every faction with a neutral, respectful one-paragraph codex blurb about its ENGINEERING/doctrine, not its politics. (b) Treat nuclear/strategic weapons as abstract, telegraphed, deterrence-flavored support powers (mutual-deterrence, defensive last resort), never as glorified city-busters or tied to real targets — the France 'Deterrence Silo' is deliberately written as a deterrent that slows enemy super-powers, not a genocide button. (c) Avoid real insignia, religious symbols, real leaders, real unit kill-counts, or real atrocity references; keep voicelines generic-military. (d) The CODEX/Encyclopedia should teach REAL strategic-resource and engineering facts (e.g. what makes an APS or an Aegis radar work, what rare-earths/lithium/uranium are used for) framed educationally, never as propaganda for any state. (e) Offer a settings toggle / map-pack that uses fully abstract sci-fi-bloc names for sensitive markets or esports, so the same balanced roster can ship 'flavor-on' or 'flavor-neutral'. Net: respectful, archetype-driven, real-doctrine-INSPIRED, real-politics-AVOIDED.
countries.detail:
HOW THIS MAPS ONTO OpenRA (engine reality + the existing design vision doc at /Users/ashishnaik/Projects/openra/design/game-design-vision.md): The roster is built to be the 'Contemporary' total-conversion analog of Red Alert's proven sub-faction pattern, which the vision doc calls 'the single most ready-to-extend structure in the whole game' (one signature unit + one signature ability per faction). Each faction here = exactly that template, so it slots onto the existing prerequisite/tech-tree, support-power, veterancy, diplomacy-stance and Encyclopedia systems with NO new engine work — only data (MiniYAML rules), Lua for a couple of bespoke powers, and the one expensive thing: sprite art.

ART-COST DISCIPLINE (the real ceiling, per the doc): 12 factions x 'one signature unit + a base set' is too much art if each faction needs a full unique roster. SCOPING RECOMMENDATION: build ONE shared modern-military base set (rifle infantry, generic MBT, generic IFV/APC, generic SAM, generic jet, harvester-equivalent, construction vehicle, refinery, power, barracks, factory, defenses) reused by ALL factions with palette/skin swaps, and give each faction only its ONE signature UNIT as bespoke 32-facing art (12 hero sprites total) plus its ONE signature BUILDING (often a reskin + new turret/FX). Buildings, support powers, research picks, diplomacy and the codex are rules/script-cheap. This is the minimum-art / maximum-design path the doc's Vectors B/C/E advocate.

DELIVERING THE 'CIVILIZATION/STELLARIS DEPTH, TONED DOWN' ASK without slowing real-time pace — three cheap layers, each plugged into an existing engine loop: (1) RESEARCH/DOCTRINE: give each faction 3-4 MUTUALLY-EXCLUSIVE doctrine choices using the EXISTING prerequisite system (e.g. Russia picks 'EW-heavy' vs 'Artillery-heavy'; Turkey picks 'cheap-swarm' vs 'Akinci-heavy'). This is the Civ 'tech-choice possibility space' but resolved in one or two in-match decisions, not a 100-turn tree — fast and legible. (2) DIPLOMACY: the engine already has player diplomacy stances; add a lightweight MARKET/TRADE building (modeled on Dune's Starport, which the doc highlights as a unique trade-economy seed) so players can trade strategic resources, form temporary pacts, or embargo — the Stellaris 'diplomacy envelope' at RTS speed. (3) STRATEGIC RESOURCES + CODEX: introduce 2-3 real-world strategic resources beyond a single ore (e.g. RARE EARTHS for advanced electronics/drones, URANIUM for the deterrent/power, OIL/LITHIUM for mobility/batteries) as secondary map deposits that gate certain doctrine units — this adds map-control decisions (the doc's wished-for 'territory layer') AND is the perfect hook for the CODEX (existing Encyclopedia widget) to teach real ore/strategic-material facts, satisfying the user's in-game-encyclopedia vision directly and cheaply.

REPLACING THE SHALLOW 'mass troops, attack/defend, repeat' LOOP: the asymmetry does the heavy lifting — because every faction's strength is also its seam (USA network node, Israel finite interceptors, Iran cheap-but-flimsy swarm, Germany slow armor, China stationary dome), matchups become about EXPLOITING the specific enemy doctrine, not out-massing. The strategic-resource map layer adds a 'where do I expand and what do I unlock' decision; the doctrine picks add a 'what kind of army am I committing to' decision; diplomacy/market adds a 'who do I deal with' decision. Together these are three real strategic decisions layered onto the fast combat loop without grand-strategy slowness.

BALANCE-AXIS SUMMARY (so no faction is universally best — they occupy different points in a design space): COST/QUALITY axis runs USA/Japan (few, elite, expensive) ↔ Iran/Turkey (many, cheap, expendable), with India/China in the middle (mass + a protected elite punch). OFFENSE/DEFENSE axis runs South Korea/USA/France (proactive tempo/strike) ↔ Israel/Japan/China (reactive denial/interception), with Russia/Germany as the attrition middle. INFORMATION axis runs UK/USA/Korea (see-first) ↔ Russia/Iran (deny-information/EW/dispersal). Every faction is strong on ONE axis and exploitable on another, which is the formal definition of asymmetric-but-fair. PAIRED COUNTERS are intentional and create a readable meta: Turkey/Iran/India/China lean on missiles+drones → hard-countered by Israel/Japan interception → which are themselves beaten by kinetic armor (Germany/Russia) and saturation (Iran) that interception can't stop → which are out-ranged by Korea/Russia artillery → which die to USA/UK/Turkey air and recon raids → which die to China/India/Japan air-defense domes. The rock-paper-scissors closes the loop, exactly as OpenRA combat is meant to.

ROSTER COMPOSITION NOTE: this is 12 factions as requested. If a smaller launch is wanted, the 6 cleanest archetypal anchors (one per balance-quadrant) are USA (network/tempo), Russia (armor/EW attrition), China (mass/denial), Israel (interception/counter), Turkey (cheap drone swarm), and Korea (sensor-to-shooter artillery) — they span the whole design space with minimal overlap; the other six deepen it. France/UK/Germany/Japan/India/Iran each add a distinct twist but share more DNA with an anchor (France~USA-versatile, UK~USA-recon/naval, Germany~Russia-durable, Japan~China/Israel-defensive-naval, India~China-protected-strike, Iran~Turkey-but-mass-ground), so they are the natural 'phase 2' additions once the anchors are balanced.

KEY FILES for whoever implements: faction definitions and per-country flavor live like RA's in mods/<contemporary>/rules/*.yaml (mirror mods/ra/rules/ structure already in the repo — vehicles.yaml, infantry.yaml, structures.yaml, aircraft.yaml, player.yaml for faction list, world.yaml); the Encyclopedia/Codex widget already exists in OpenRA.Mods.Common/Widgets for the strategic-resource lore; support powers and the deterrence/barrage/interception specials follow the existing support-power + Warhead/Projectile traits in OpenRA.Mods.Common/Traits and /Warheads; diplomacy stances are already engine-level. No determinism-sensitive new sim systems are required beyond standard trait composition.

resources.economyModel:
THREE-PILLAR MODEL: "1 fluid currency + 3 strategic stockpiles + 2 soft meters + a supply-line overlay." The deliberate sweet spot between StarCraft's 2-resource simplicity and Civ's 20-resource spreadsheet.

WHY THIS SHAPE (core thesis): the current loop is shallow because ALL units draw from ONE undifferentiated credit pool, so every economic decision collapses to "do I have enough cash?" One axis = one question. The fix is NOT "add ten ores" (spreadsheet hell, and the engine only cleanly supports ~7 tile resource indices anyway). The fix is to make a few resources MEAN different things by gating different DOCTRINES of the tech tree, so holding a deposit is a strategic commitment.

LAYERS:
(1) CREDITS — the one fluid currency. Fed by two ABUNDANT open-field resources, Petroleum and Iron, in classic harvest-under-threat fields. Pays for everything baseline. Engine: both map to the single PlayerResources Cash pool via ResourceValues, exactly like Ore/Gems today. Zero new systems.
(2) THREE STRATEGIC STOCKPILES — Rare Earths, Uranium, Lithium. Separate integer counters, NOT credits. Scarce: a handful of fixed central/contested DEPOSIT tiles per map. You don't spend them down each tick; you accumulate small amounts that act as PREREQUISITE + slow-UPKEEP gates on three distinct top-tier doctrine branches (drones/EW, nuclear, batteries/directed-energy). This is where territory becomes strategy: you can win on credits with a conventional army, but you CANNOT field the high-tech edge without physically holding the deposit. Engine: a thin PlayerStrategicResources counter cloned from PlayerResources; tech gates via a generalized GrantConditionOnPlayerResources ("requires >= N RareEarths").
(3) FOOD/WATER — a soft population/upkeep meter (like Power): buildings raise it, units consume it, exceeding it penalizes production/healing. Adds expansion tension with no micromanagement. Engine: reuse the PowerManager pattern verbatim.
(4) SUPPLY LINES — strategic stockpiles must be TRUCKED from deposit to a Stockpile building (the existing Harvester+Refinery+dock loop reskinned as convoys). Cut the convoy and you choke enemy high-tech production without touching their base = the "interesting defense"/economic-warfare depth the vision asks for, nearly free in art.

COUNT JUSTIFICATION: 1 number watched constantly (credits) + 3 occasionally (stockpiles) + 2 passive bars (food/water, power) — under the ~5-7 working-memory ceiling that separates tension from tedium. Silicon, Titanium, Copper, Bauxite, Natural Gas, Cobalt, Phosphate are NOT counters — they live in the CODEX as flavor behind buildings/units. Educate via codex breadth; gate via mechanic narrowness.

FACTION DIFFERENTIATION (the "real countries" ask): factions share the resource set but differ in EFFICIENCY/ACCESS. China: Rare-Earth/Titanium doctrine discounts (mirrors real ~90% processing dominance), drone/EW unique units. Russia: Uranium/aerospace discounts. USA/EU: cheap conventional but import-dependent (need more deposits). A Chile/DRC/Australia-flavored faction: passive stockpile generation from fewer deposits. Same map plays differently per country — strategic-use differentiation without a combinatorial balance blowup. All integer, deterministic, lock-step safe.
resources.executiveSummary:
I designed a real-strategic-resource economy and wrote its codex, grounded in (a) the verbatim vision, (b) the actual engine (tile-based ResourceLayer supporting ~7 resource indices each mapping to the single PlayerResources Cash pool; the existing Harvester/Refinery/dock loop; GrantConditionOnPlayerResources for resource-gated tech; the existing Encyclopedia widget at OpenRA.Mods.Common/Traits/Encyclopedia.cs + Widgets/Logic/EncyclopediaLogic.cs), and (c) fresh 2025-2026 web research on critical-minerals geopolitics.

Diagnosis: the loop is shallow because ONE undifferentiated credit pool means ONE economic question. Adding many ores just creates tedium (and the engine caps cleanly around 7 tile resources). The fix is a THREE-PILLAR model: ONE fluid currency (Credits, fed by abundant Petroleum + Iron in classic open fields, so the harvest-under-threat loop survives untouched), THREE scarce strategic STOCKPILES (Rare Earths, Uranium, Lithium) that are NOT spent like cash but gate three distinct top-tier DOCTRINES (drones/EW, nuclear, batteries/directed-energy), plus a soft Food/Water meter (reuses the Power pattern). A supply-line overlay (reskinned harvester convoys) makes strategic deposits truckable and cuttable, delivering interesting defense, territorial control, and economic warfare for almost no art cost.

The player watches ONE number constantly and THREE occasionally — under the working-memory ceiling, so it reads as tension, not spreadsheet. Everything else real (silicon/Taiwan, titanium/aerospace, copper/electrification, cobalt/DRC, phosphate/food) lives in the CODEX as building/unit lore, teaching real facts without adding counters. Factions differ by resource EFFICIENCY/ACCESS rather than resource set, so the same map plays differently per country. All integer-based, no floats/DateTime/Random in sim, fully lock-step safe. Per-resource codex entries with verified 2025-2026 facts are in the resources array.
recommendations: SHIP THE MINIMUM VIABLE TENSION FIRST: 1 currency (Credits via Petroleum+Iron) + exactly 1 strategic stockpile (Rare Earths gating a drone/EW doctrine). Proves the 'territory = tech access' loop with one new counter before adding Uranium/Lithium. Nearly free: ResourceLayer supports a 3rd index and GrantConditionOnPlayerResources already gates tech on a player resource counter.

REUSE, DON'T BUILD: strategic-stockpile counters = a thin clone of PlayerResources.cs; supply convoys = the existing Harvester+Refinery+IDockHost loop reskinned (Harvester.cs/Refinery.cs, HarvestResource.cs/FindAndDeliverResources.cs); Food/Water = a second PowerManager meter; tech gates = GrantConditionOnPlayerResources generalized to non-cash resources. Keeps everything integer and deterministic, no new sim primitives that risk desyncs.

CAP STOCKPILES AT THREE, FOREVER. Don't add Copper/Silicon/Titanium/Cobalt as separate piles — that's the spreadsheet trap and breaks the ~7-index limit. They belong in the CODEX as building/unit flavor only. The design hinges on educate-via-codex-breadth, gate-via-mechanic-narrowness.

MAKE THE CODEX DIEGETIC: surface a resource's codex card the first time the player mines that deposit or unlocks a unit needing it (Encyclopedia widget exists in mods/cnc + mods/d2k chrome/encyclopedia.yaml). A real fact delivered at the moment of strategic relevance teaches without a wiki dump.

DIFFERENTIATE FACTIONS BY RESOURCE EFFICIENCY, NOT SET: China gets Rare-Earth/Titanium discounts, Russia Uranium/aerospace, USA/EU cheap-conventional-but-import-dependent, a Chile/DRC/Australia faction passive stockpile generation. Same map, different economy per country = the vision's strategic-use differentiation without a combinatorial balance nightmare.

GATE WITH UPKEEP, NOT JUST UNLOCK: nuclear silos/drone hangars slowly DRAIN their stockpile while active, so losing the deposit visibly degrades your high-tech edge over time. This turns 'I unlocked drones' into the ongoing 'can I keep them fed?' tension that fixes the static single-currency loop.

VALIDATE EARLY WITH make check: each new resource needs a ResourceLayer entry + ResourceValues mapping + ResourceRenderer sequence; the YAML lint rules in OpenRA.Mods.Common/Lint catch dangling refs at build time — add codex/Encyclopedia entries in the same pass to avoid orphaned references.
resources.detail:
ENGINE-GROUNDING (verified against the repo, so this is buildable):
- Resources are TILE-based via OpenRA.Mods.Common/Traits/World/ResourceLayer.cs (ResourceTypeInfo carries a byte ResourceIndex; ~7 distinct types practical). Each maps to one integer Cash value in PlayerResources.Info.ResourceValues (FrozenDictionary<string,int>); Refinery.cs AcceptResources() converts harvested units to cash through that dictionary. So 'multiple ores -> credits' (Petroleum+Iron) is solved today (two ResourceValues entries). 'Resources that are NOT credits' (the 3 stockpiles) need a parallel counter trait cloned from PlayerResources — the only genuinely new code, small and integer-only.
- Tech gating on a resource quantity exists: GrantConditionOnPlayerResources grants a condition at a cash threshold; generalizing it to a named stockpile is the mechanism for 'requires >= N Rare Earths.' Prerequisite + condition system = no new sim concept.
- Supply lines = the existing Harvester/Refinery/IDockHost loop; a convoy is a harvester carrying a strategic load deposit->Stockpile, interceptable to deny upkeep. HarvesterAttackNotifier.cs already provides 'your convoy is under attack' feedback.
- Food/Water = a second soft meter on the PowerManager pattern; integer, ITick, determinism-safe.
- Codex: Encyclopedia.cs + EncyclopediaLogic.cs + mods/*/chrome/encyclopedia.yaml already render lore entries with art.

DETERMINISM COMPLIANCE: every quantity is an integer counter or threshold; no float/double, no DateTime/Random, nothing reads UI/wall-clock from world.Tick(). All meters are integer ITick accumulators XOR-able into the sync hash — mandatory under lock-step.

HOW IT FIXES THE SHALLOW LOOP (mapped to the 5 loops in design/game-design-vision.md):
- Economic: was 1 resource -> 1 question. Now Credits keep the fast harvest loop, while 3 contested central deposits make map control a TECH-ACCESS choice, not just income.
- Combat: counters gain an economic precondition — 'enemy is teching to drones' is readable because they had to seize a Rare-Earth deposit and run a convoy; scouting the economy = scouting the tech.
- Support-power: superweapons become doctrine payoffs gated by Uranium (nuke) / Lithium (rail/DEW) / Rare Earth (drone swarm) — earned by sustained territory, not a bare timer.
- This is the 'sixth loop' the design doc wants (a territory/economic-warfare layer), delivered cheaply by reskinning existing systems.

WHY NOT MORE RESOURCES: Civ tolerates 20+ because it's turn-based (unlimited time to read a tile). Real-time must be glanceable under combat stress; the comfortable simultaneous-resource ceiling is ~5-7. My model = 1 constant + 3 occasional + 2 passive bars. Everything else real (silicon/Taiwan >90% of advanced chips, titanium/Russia-China aerospace grip, copper/~50% demand growth to 2040, cobalt/DRC, phosphate-potash food weaponization, gas/Hormuz) is taught via CODEX entries on buildings/units, giving full educational breadth with zero added counters. That is the central trade.

CODEX TEMPLATE: each entry has three beats — REAL ROLE / IN-GAME ROLE / THE HOOK (one verified surprising fact). All hooks in the resources array are from 2025-2026 reporting (USGS, IEA/CSIS, EIA, World Nuclear Association, defense/trade press), current as of the research date.

resources.name: Petroleum (Oil)
resources.realWorldRole: The master fuel of industrial militaries: powers tanks, ships, jets, and logistics. ~34% of global crude trade and ~20% of world oil consumption transits a single chokepoint, the Strait of Hormuz, making sea-lane control a strategic act in itself.
resources.inGameRole: ABUNDANT credit-feeder #1. Harvested from open-field pump/derrick tiles in the classic harvest-under-threat loop; converts directly to Credits via ResourceValues. Also a soft fuel-upkeep flavor for vehicle/air doctrines. The bread-and-butter economy a new player can rely on alone.
resources.codexHook: In 2025 roughly 34% of all seaborne crude oil and about 20% of global LNG squeezed through the Strait of Hormuz — a waterway ~33 km wide at its narrowest. One blocked strait can shock the entire planet's energy price.

resources.name: Iron / Steel Ore
resources.realWorldRole: The literal backbone of conventional war: hulls, armor, guns, rails, reinforced concrete. Unglamorous and abundant, but no army moves or fortifies without it. Steel output has been a proxy for industrial-war capacity since WWII.
resources.inGameRole: ABUNDANT credit-feeder #2. The second open-field resource converting to Credits, feeding all conventional units/buildings and base defenses. Pairs with Petroleum so the baseline economy has two harvestable fields — redundancy that keeps the fast RTS loop intact while the strategic deposits stay scarce and contested.
resources.codexHook: Steel is the most recycled material on Earth by tonnage — a modern tank or warship is largely re-smelted scrap. Industrial war is, quite literally, melted-down history fighting itself.

resources.name: Rare Earth Elements
resources.realWorldRole: Seventeen metals (neodymium, dysprosium, samarium...) that make the high-performance permanent magnets inside precision-guided munitions, missile guidance, stealth tech, radar, drone motors, and electric actuators. The single most weaponizable mineral dependency in modern defense.
resources.inGameRole: STRATEGIC STOCKPILE #1 — gates the ADVANCED ELECTRONICS / DRONE / ELECTRONIC-WARFARE doctrine. Held as a separate counter from a few contested deposit tiles; required as prerequisite + slow upkeep to build and sustain drones, EW jammers, smart munitions, and stealth units. Lose the deposit and your high-tech swarm starves. China-flavored factions get a discount here.
resources.codexHook: China refines over 85% of the world's rare earths and makes ~90% of high-performance NdFeB magnets — the magnets inside Western fighter jets, submarines, and guided missiles. In April 2025 it put export controls on 7 of the 17 elements, and analysts say a US supply chain won't fully stand up before 2027 at the earliest.

resources.name: Uranium
resources.realWorldRole: Fuels nuclear reactors and is the fissile basis of nuclear weapons. Raw ore is only step one — the real chokepoint is ENRICHMENT and conversion, which is geopolitically concentrated. Naval reactors also let submarines and carriers run for decades without refueling.
resources.inGameRole: STRATEGIC STOCKPILE #2 — gates the NUCLEAR doctrine: reactor buildings (a big power/economy boost) and the nuclear-strike superweapon, plus nuclear-powered naval units. Scarce deposit-fed counter; the nuke superweapon is a doctrine PAYOFF earned by sustained territorial control, not a bare timer. Russia-flavored factions get a discount.
resources.codexHook: Kazakhstan mines ~40% of the world's uranium, but Russia's Rosatom controls ~38% of global uranium conversion and ~46% of enrichment capacity — so even uranium-rich nations can depend on a rival just to make the ore usable. Mining the rock is the easy part; enriching it is the real power.

resources.name: Lithium
resources.realWorldRole: The energy-storage metal: batteries for everything from soldier radios and drones to grid power and electric vehicles. As militaries electrify (silent EVs, directed-energy weapons, portable power), battery supply becomes a frontline logistics concern. Demand is forecast to roughly triple within a decade.
resources.inGameRole: STRATEGIC STOCKPILE #3 — gates the ENERGY / DIRECTED-ENERGY / MOBILE-POWER doctrine: railguns and laser/DEW defenses, silent electric scout vehicles, and battery-buffered bases that resist power-knockout. Deposit-fed counter that turns 'I have power' into 'I can deploy beam weapons and stay dark.'
resources.codexHook: Australia and Chile alone supply well over half the world's lithium, yet by 2030 the market is projected to be ~20% in deficit — demand is outrunning every new mine. The metal that powers the quiet, electric future is already running short.

resources.name: Food & Water
resources.realWorldRole: The oldest strategic resource and the one most often weaponized: fertilizer (phosphate/potash), grain exports, and fresh water decide whether a population — and an army — can be sustained. Blockading food or fertilizer is 'war by other means,' and Canada alone supplies ~90% of US potash imports.
resources.inGameRole: SOFT POPULATION/UPKEEP METER (not a harvested pile) — like Power. Farms/desalination raise the cap; every unit consumes some; exceed it and production and healing slow. Adds an expansion/sustain tension (bigger army demands more territory to feed it) with zero micromanagement, since it's a passive bar, not a convoy.
resources.codexHook: Fertilizer is so strategic it gets sanctioned and exempted like a weapon: when the US tariffed fertilizer in April 2025 it pointedly LEFT Russian fertilizer duty-free. You can starve a nation without firing a shot — just choke its phosphate and potash.

resources.name: Silicon (Semiconductors)
resources.realWorldRole: Refined silicon becomes the chips that run every guidance computer, sensor, radar, and AI targeting system. The strategic chokepoint isn't the sand — it's advanced FABRICATION, which is extraordinarily concentrated, making chip foundries a top-tier geopolitical prize.
resources.inGameRole: CODEX-ONLY (no counter). It is the LORE behind the 'Fabrication Plant' / advanced-tech-center building that the drone and EW doctrines build through. Teaches the chip-war story at the exact moment a player unlocks high-tech production, without adding a resource to track — the model's educate-via-codex, gate-via-mechanic principle in action.
resources.codexHook: Taiwan makes over 60% of the world's chips and more than 90% of the most ADVANCED ones; TSMC alone holds ~64-70% of the contract-foundry market. A single island, smaller than many countries' provinces, is a load-bearing pillar of every modern military's electronics.

resources.name: Titanium
resources.realWorldRole: The strong-yet-light metal of aerospace: jet airframes, engine parts, missile bodies, submarine hulls. About half of a modern fighter's structure can depend on titanium alloys, and the refined 'sponge' supply is geopolitically concentrated.
resources.inGameRole: CODEX-ONLY (no counter). It is the LORE behind the 'Aerospace Works' building and explains why advanced aircraft cost more and tech deeper than ground units — a flavor justification for the air doctrine's price/tier. Russia/China-flavored factions reference it for their aerospace discounts. Educates on the aerospace supply squeeze with no pile to manage.
resources.codexHook: Russia and China between them now supply roughly three-quarters of the world's titanium metal — China's share leapt from ~40% in 2019 to over 75% by 2025. Boeing and Airbus historically bought a third to half of their titanium from Russia, so the metal in Western airliners often started in a rival's furnace.

visual.executiveSummary: Target a "modern diorama" look I'll call HD-Pixel/Lite-HD-2D: keep OpenRA's top-down RTS readability and a deliberately retro silhouette language, but replace blurry upscaled palette-SHP sprites with clean, high-resolution sprites rendered from 3D models, lit consistently, and composited over modernized terrain with subtle modern post (soft shadows, light bloom, gentle depth cueing). The single most important constraint, confirmed by the C&C Remastered team, is counter-intuitive: at RTS camera distance, MORE realism/detail reads WORSE. So the aesthetic target is "clean and bold, not photoreal" — chunky readable silhouettes, strong faction color, restrained detail. The hard production problem (32 rotationally consistent facings + animations + palette team-color remap) has exactly one robust solution at scale: a 3D-model -> orthographic turntable render -> downscale -> indexed-palette pipeline in Blender. This is literally how Westwood made the originals and how the Remaster was re-derived; it gives perfect rotational/animation consistency for free. AI image generation (GPT-image/SDXL) is structurally bad at rotational consistency (style drift, silhouette flips, palette drift across angles are its #1 documented failure) and must NOT be the unit pipeline — but it is excellent for the things that are single-angle: concept exploration, unit/building cameos, hero/loading/menu art, Codex illustrations, and faction iconography. Recommend a hybrid split: Blender renders everything that moves in the world; AI accelerates everything seen from one angle. Crucially, OpenRA ALREADY ships the engine support needed: a real-time voxel/3D-model renderer (used by the Tiberian Sun mod, with configurable lighting), a non-palette PNG sprite-sheet loader, and a working TiberianDawnHD mod that loads C&C Remastered 4K assets with a runtime classic/HD toggle. So this is an asset-and-art-direction effort, not an engine rewrite.
keyFindings: READABILITY BEATS REALISM at RTS zoom — this is the load-bearing rule. The C&C Remastered team (Petroglyph + Lemon Sky) found that making the redrawn 4K units MORE realistic made them HARDER to read from the game's fixed top-down angle; they deliberately simplified. Tanya ended up 'bulky, almost like a muscular guy' because exaggerated, chunky forms read better than accurate ones. Tooth and Tail is praised for 'perfect clarity on what the unit is and what it does with almost zero overlap.' Design rule for this project: silhouette-first. Every unit must be identifiable as a black silhouette at 100% zoom. Detail is a budget you spend on the silhouette and the faction color, not on rivets.

The aesthetic target is a NAMED, achievable style, not vague 'HD.' Three reference poles: (1) Faithful-retro / HD pixel (Wargroove, Tooth and Tail) — hand-pixeled, charming, cheap to read, but labor-heavy and caps at low detail. (2) Clean high-res sprite (C&C Remastered, They Are Billions = 'a high-resolution take on the original StarCraft', AoE Definitive Editions) — 3D-rendered down to crisp 2D, the natural fit for OpenRA's scale and the de-blur goal. (3) HD-2D (Octopath Traveler) — 2D billboard sprites in a 3D-lit world with dynamic lighting, soft shadows, depth-of-field, tilt-shift. RECOMMEND landing between (2) and a light (3): clean rendered sprites = the de-blur; a restrained HD-2D post layer (real-time soft drop shadows, gentle bloom on muzzle flash/energy, subtle ambient occlusion at unit bases, light depth cue) = the 'modern revamp' that makes it feel contemporary without a single new unit frame.

The '32 rotationally-consistent facings' requirement is the entire reason AI generation fails and 3D rendering wins. AI turnaround tools' #1 documented complaint is exactly rotational inconsistency: 'outfits change, palettes drift, silhouettes flip' between angles; 'generate the same character twice and you get two completely different art styles.' Even with LoRA + ControlNet/OpenPose + seed locking it's fragile, per-asset babysitting, and still drifts — fatal when one tank needs 32 angles x N animation frames that must register pixel-perfectly as it rotates. A 3D model rendered on a turntable is rotationally PERFECT by construction: same mesh, same lights, just the camera/turntable steps 360/32 = 11.25 degrees. This is non-negotiable for in-world units.

OpenRA ALREADY has the engine plumbing — this is an art/asset task, not an engine rewrite. Confirmed in-repo: (a) a real-time voxel/3D-model renderer with configurable lighting (OpenRA.Mods.Cnc/Traits/Render/RenderVoxels.cs + WithVoxel* traits, used by the Tiberian Sun mod — LightPitch/LightYaw/Ambient/Diffuse are already data-driven knobs); (b) a non-palette RGBA PNG sprite-sheet path (OpenRA.Mods.Common/SpriteLoaders/PngSheetLoader.cs) so HD sprites needn't be 8-bit palette-indexed; (c) a shipping TiberianDawnHD mod that loads C&C Remastered 4K assets with a runtime classic/HD content toggle. Sequences already declare 'Facings: 32 / UseClassicFacings: True' per animation (mods/ra/sequences/vehicles.yaml). So HD assets drop into the existing sequence/SHP-or-PNG system; team color still works via the palette-remap path.

Team color is a HARD pipeline constraint that shapes the whole render setup. OpenRA recolors factions by remapping a reserved palette ramp (PlayerColorRemap / RRGB ramp), and Wargroove-style palette swapping is the genre norm. In the 3D pipeline you must author the team-color regions as a FLAT, pre-decided color ramp on the model (an unlit 'remap' material channel) so that after downscale those pixels land exactly on the reserved indices. Practically: render two passes (full-color RGBA beauty pass + a separate remap-mask pass) OR bake the remap region to magenta-ramp indices. This is solvable but must be designed in from frame one, not bolted on.

AI image generation is genuinely the RIGHT tool for everything seen from ONE angle — don't throw it out, scope it. Strong fit: concept/silhouette exploration to lock a unit's look before modeling; the sidebar build-icon cameos; faction crests/flags/iconography; loading screens, menu/hero art, mission briefing stills; and especially the CODEX/Encyclopedia illustrations (real ores, real military tech) where a single beautiful plate per entry is ideal and rotational consistency is irrelevant. OpenRA already has the Encyclopedia widget (OpenRA.Mods.Common/Widgets/Logic/EncyclopediaLogic.cs + mods/*/chrome/encyclopedia.yaml) to host this art.
recommendations: ADOPT THE HYBRID PIPELINE EXPLICITLY. Blender 3D-render pipeline = canonical source for EVERY in-world animated asset (units, vehicles, infantry, buildings, turrets, projectiles, explosions). AI generation = single-angle assets only (concept art, build-icon cameos, faction iconography, loading/menu/hero art, Codex plates). Never let AI produce the 32-facing rotation set. Write this split into the art bible so contributors don't 'just AI a tank.'

STANDARDIZE THE BLENDER TURNTABLE RIG as a committed, scripted tool. Orthographic camera, fixed OpenRA-matching pitch (the classic C&C 3/4 top-down, roughly 30-35deg from horizontal — match existing SHP angle so new and old assets coexist during transition). Parent the model to a turntable empty; animate a 360deg Z-rotation; render 32 frames for facings (UseClassicFacings spacing) x each animation's frame count. Use a headless `blender --background --python render_facings.py` script checked into the repo (design/ or tools/) so renders are reproducible and batchable on any contributor's machine or CI. Reference proven addons (Foozle's Blender directional-sprite scripts, DirectionalSpriteBatchRender) rather than hand-rolling.

LOCK LIGHTING AND SCALE ONCE, GLOBALLY. One shared 3-point lighting setup (key/fill/rim) and one world-unit-to-pixel scale for the entire faction roster, so every unit looks like it lives in the same world and de-blurs consistently. Mirror the rig's light direction into the engine's model-render LightPitch/LightYaw/Ambient/Diffuse values (already exposed in RenderVoxels.cs) so any real-time 3D-rendered units match the pre-baked sprites.

BUILD TEAM COLOR INTO THE RENDER FROM FRAME ONE. Author each unit's team-color region as a flat unlit material on a dedicated 'remap' ramp. Render a beauty pass + a remap-mask pass; in post (ImageMagick/Python in the same render script) quantize the remap pixels onto OpenRA's reserved palette ramp so PlayerColorRemap keeps working. Validate with `./utility.sh ra --check-yaml` and an in-engine team-color spot check before committing a unit.

DE-BLUR VIA RESOLUTION + POST, NOT JUST BIGGER SPRITES. Render sprites at 2x-4x the classic pixel footprint through the PngSheetLoader (RGBA, escape 8-bit palette banding where art benefits), THEN add the cheap 'modern' layer in-engine: real-time soft drop shadows under units, subtle ambient-occlusion contact darkening at unit bases, restrained bloom on muzzle flashes/energy weapons/explosions, and a gentle depth/atmosphere cue. This is the 'retro but revamped' feel and most of it is engine-side shader/trait work that upgrades ALL existing art at once, before a single new unit is drawn.

PROTOTYPE ON ONE FACTION + ONE BIOME FIRST (vertical slice). Pick ~6 units (1 harvester-equiv, 1 light vehicle, 1 tank, 2 infantry, 1 aircraft) + 4 buildings for a single modern faction, take them fully through Blender->sprite->team-color->in-engine, and ship them next to classic assets using the proven TiberianDawnHD-style runtime toggle. Get readability sign-off at real zoom BEFORE scaling the pipeline to all factions. This de-risks the silhouette/readability rule cheaply.

MODERNIZE THE HUD/CODEX TOWARD 'CLEAN MILITARY HUD,' KEEPING READABILITY KING. Direction: flatter panels, a tightened grid, crisp vector/SDF UI icons, a restrained 1-2 accent-color-per-faction scheme, legible modern sans for data with the retro display face reserved for headers. Keep the command-sidebar muscle memory intact. For the Codex/Encyclopedia (real ores + real military tech), use the existing Encyclopedia widget: left nav tree (Resources / Units / Buildings / Factions), big AI-generated hero plate per entry, structured stat block, and cross-links — this is the natural home for the Civ/Stellaris-style depth surfaced as readable reference, and its art is exactly the single-angle case where AI shines.
risks: Scope/labor blowout: a full modern roster of 3D models is real 3D-artist work. Each unit = model + rig + animation set, then x32 facings. This is the same cost ceiling the user already flagged for sprites — 3D front-loads it into modeling but pays it back in perfect consistency and trivial re-renders (new angle, new lighting, new resolution = re-run the script). Mitigate by sharing base meshes across same-class units (kit-bashing real military hardware) and prioritizing the vertical slice.

Readability regression: HD detail and modern post (bloom, shadows, AO) can easily HURT gameplay clarity — the exact trap C&C Remastered had to design around. If unit silhouettes stop being instantly distinguishable at combat zoom, the game gets worse despite looking 'better.' Mitigate with a hard silhouette-test gate (every unit must be ID-able as a flat black shape at 100% zoom) and keep all post effects restrained/toggleable.

Team-color failure mode: if remap regions aren't authored as flat ramps and quantized carefully, downscaling/anti-aliasing bleeds team color into adjacent pixels and PlayerColorRemap produces muddy edges or mis-tinted units. This silently breaks faction identification in multiplayer. Mitigate with the dedicated remap-mask pass and an automated post-render validation.

Mixed-asset visual incoherence during transition: shipping new HD units beside classic blurry SHP looks worse than either alone. The classic/HD toggle (TiberianDawnHD precedent) avoids forcing a half-converted state on players, but biome/terrain must be modernized in lockstep with units or the diorama breaks. Convert by complete faction + matching terrain set, not piecemeal.

AI-art licensing/style-coherence and GPLv3 hygiene: AI-generated Codex/cameo art must be style-locked (one prompt/LoRA recipe) or the game's single-angle art will look like a random asset pack, and its provenance/licensing must be compatible with the project's libre/GPLv3 stance and contributor terms. Mitigate with a fixed AI style guide and a clear asset-licensing policy before accepting AI art into the repo.

Performance/memory: HD RGBA sheets and any real-time 3D-model rendering cost VRAM and load time — OpenRA's own HD experiment notes performance/memory/load are unoptimized and recommends a dedicated GPU. Budget for sheet atlasing, mip/zoom LODs, and keep an option to run classic assets on low-end machines.
