VISUAL DIRECTION SUMMARY ("retro but revamped", de-blurred)

1) THE AESTHETIC TARGET
Name it so the team can aim: "HD-Pixel diorama" — clean, high-resolution, 3D-rendered-to-2D sprites (the de-blur), with a restrained HD-2D post layer (soft real-time shadows, contact AO, gentle bloom, light depth cue) to read as contemporary. It sits between the C&C Remastered / They Are Billions / AoE-DE pole (clean rendered sprites at RTS scale) and the Octopath HD-2D pole (2D sprites in a 3D-lit world). It explicitly is NOT photoreal Steel Division and NOT hand-pixeled Wargroove/Tooth-and-Tail (too detail-capped and labor-heavy for a full modern roster). The retro DNA is preserved in the camera angle, the chunky silhouette language, and strong palette-swapped faction color.

THE GOVERNING RULE (from C&C Remastered's own postmortem): at this fixed top-down RTS angle, more realism reads WORSE. So: silhouette-first, exaggerated/chunky forms, detail spent on the outline and faction color, never on photoreal rivets. Every unit must pass a "flat black silhouette at 100% zoom" identification test. They Are Billions is literally 'a high-resolution take on the original StarCraft'; Tooth and Tail is the clarity benchmark. That tension between detail and readability is the whole art problem, and readability wins every time it conflicts.

2) WHY THE PIPELINE MUST BE 3D-RENDER, NOT AI (the 32-facing problem)
The hard requirement — 32 rotationally consistent facings + animation frames + palette team-color remap — is exactly where AI generation structurally fails. Documented #1 complaint of AI turnaround tools: silhouettes flip, outfits change, palettes drift between angles; re-running gives a different style. LoRA + ControlNet/OpenPose + seed-locking only mitigate it and still drift — unworkable when a rotating tank's 32 angles must register pixel-perfectly. A 3D model on a turntable is rotationally perfect by construction (same mesh/lights, camera steps 11.25deg). This is exactly how Westwood built the originals (3D render -> downscale -> indexed palette; they moved to voxels in Tiberian Sun) and how the Remaster was re-derived.

3) THE RECOMMENDED HYBRID SPLIT
- Blender 3D pipeline = canonical for EVERYTHING in the world that moves/rotates: units, infantry, vehicles, buildings, turrets, projectiles, explosions. Reproducible scripted rig (`blender --background --python render_facings.py`, checked into the repo): orthographic camera at OpenRA's classic ~30-35deg pitch; model parented to a turntable empty; 360deg Z animation; render 32 facings x animation frames; one global 3-point lighting rig and one world->pixel scale for the whole roster; beauty pass + remap-mask pass; post-quantize remap pixels onto OpenRA's reserved palette ramp; atlas via PngSheetLoader (RGBA, no 8-bit banding). Proven prior art: Foozle's Blender directional-sprite scripts, DirectionalSpriteBatchRender, clintbellanger's isometric-tile method.
- AI generation (GPT-image/SDXL) = single-angle assets ONLY: concept/silhouette exploration to lock a look before modeling; sidebar build-icon cameos; faction crests/flags/iconography; loading/menu/hero/briefing art; and the Codex/Encyclopedia illustrations for real ores + real military tech. Lock one AI style recipe so these don't look like a random pack; settle licensing for GPLv3/libre before accepting AI art into the repo.

4) ENGINE REALITY (good news — minimal engine work)
OpenRA already supports this. In-repo: a real-time voxel/3D-model renderer with data-driven lighting (OpenRA.Mods.Cnc/Traits/Render/RenderVoxels.cs exposes LightPitch=50deg, LightYaw=240deg, LightAmbientColor, LightDiffuseColor, Scale; plus WithVoxelBody/Turret/Barrel/WalkerBody, used by the Tiberian Sun mod); a non-palette RGBA PNG sprite path (OpenRA.Mods.Common/SpriteLoaders/PngSheetLoader.cs); a shipping TiberianDawnHD mod that loads C&C Remastered 4K assets with a runtime classic/HD toggle. Sequences already declare per-animation 'Facings: 32 / UseClassicFacings: True' (mods/ra/sequences/vehicles.yaml). So HD assets drop into the existing sequence system, team color keeps working via PlayerColorRemap (OpenRA.Game/Graphics/PlayerColorRemap.cs), and you can ship new HD units beside classic ones using the proven toggle. Mirror the Blender rig's light direction into the engine LightPitch/LightYaw so any real-time-rendered 3D units match the pre-baked sprites.

5) THE 'REVAMP' LAYER (upgrades all art at once, engine-side)
Before drawing one new unit, add restrained modern post as traits/shaders: real-time soft drop shadows, base-contact ambient occlusion, bloom on muzzle flash/energy/explosions, gentle depth/atmosphere. This is most of the 'modern' feel and it lifts existing assets immediately. Render new sprites at 2-4x the classic footprint for the de-blur.

6) UI/HUD + CODEX MODERNIZATION
HUD direction: 'clean military HUD' — flatter panels, tightened grid, crisp vector/SDF icons, 1-2 faction accent colors, legible modern sans for data with a retro display face reserved for headers; keep the command-sidebar layout/muscle memory. Codex: reuse the existing Encyclopedia widget (OpenRA.Mods.Common/Widgets/Logic/EncyclopediaLogic.cs; Encyclopedia trait at OpenRA.Mods.Common/Traits/Encyclopedia.cs; chrome at mods/cnc/chrome/encyclopedia.yaml, mods/d2k/chrome/encyclopedia.yaml). Layout: left nav tree (Resources / Units / Buildings / Factions), a large AI-generated hero plate per entry (the single-angle case where AI excels), structured stat block, cross-links. This is the natural home for the real-ore + real-military-tech reference and the Civ/Stellaris-style depth the vision wants, surfaced as readable encyclopedia rather than slow grand-strategy.

7) PRACTICAL ROLLOUT
Vertical slice first: one modern faction (~6 units: harvester-equiv, light vehicle, tank, 2 infantry, aircraft + 4 buildings) + one matching terrain/biome, fully through Blender->sprite->team-color->in-engine, shipped beside classic via the runtime toggle. Get readability sign-off at real combat zoom BEFORE scaling the pipeline. Convert by complete faction+terrain sets (never piecemeal) to avoid mixed-asset incoherence. Share base meshes across same-class units (kit-bash real military hardware) to contain the modeling cost ceiling.

RELEVANT IN-REPO FILES (absolute paths):
- /Users/ashishnaik/Projects/openra/OpenRA.Mods.Cnc/Traits/Render/RenderVoxels.cs (real-time 3D-model render + lighting knobs)
- /Users/ashishnaik/Projects/openra/OpenRA.Mods.Cnc/Graphics/Voxel.cs, VoxelLoader.cs, ModelRenderable.cs (3D model rendering)
- /Users/ashishnaik/Projects/openra/OpenRA.Mods.Common/SpriteLoaders/PngSheetLoader.cs (HD RGBA sprite path)
- /Users/ashishnaik/Projects/openra/OpenRA.Game/Graphics/PlayerColorRemap.cs (team-color remap)
- /Users/ashishnaik/Projects/openra/OpenRA.Mods.Common/UtilityCommands/ConvertSpriteToPngCommand.cs, DumpSequenceSheetsCommand.cs, PngSheetImport/ExportMetadataCommand.cs (sprite tooling)
- /Users/ashishnaik/Projects/openra/mods/ra/sequences/vehicles.yaml (32-facing sequence declarations)
- /Users/ashishnaik/Projects/openra/OpenRA.Mods.Common/Widgets/Logic/EncyclopediaLogic.cs + /Users/ashishnaik/Projects/openra/OpenRA.Mods.Common/Traits/Encyclopedia.cs (Codex host)
- /Users/ashishnaik/Projects/openra/mods/cnc/chrome/encyclopedia.yaml, /Users/ashishnaik/Projects/openra/mods/d2k/chrome/encyclopedia.yaml (Codex layout)
External precedent to study: OpenRA/TiberianDawnHD mod (runtime classic/HD asset toggle).

precedents.name: Command & Conquer Remastered Collection (Petroglyph + Lemon Sky Studios)
precedents.whatTheyDid: Hand-redrew every unit/building/infantry/terrain sprite at 4K with new animations, derived from 3D, with a one-key toggle between remastered and original visuals. Deliberately SIMPLIFIED detail because the fixed top-down RTS angle made realistic units hard to read (e.g. Tanya made 'bulky, almost like a muscular guy').
precedents.outcome: Widely praised as the gold-standard RTS remaster; proved you can de-blur the classics while preserving 'the look as it existed in memories.' OpenRA's own TiberianDawnHD mod now loads these exact 4K assets with a runtime classic/HD toggle.
precedents.lessonForUs: This IS the target and the proof of feasibility. Copy two things: (a) clean-not-realistic at RTS zoom, and (b) the runtime classic/HD toggle so HD and legacy assets coexist during a multi-faction conversion.

precedents.name: Octopath Traveler / HD-2D (Square Enix CBU II + Acquire)
precedents.whatTheyDid: Combined 2D billboard pixel sprites with fully 3D-lit environments using dynamic lighting, real-time character shadows from added point lights, depth-of-field, and tilt-shift to create a diorama look.
precedents.outcome: Defined a whole commercially successful art-style category; widely emulated. Made low-res-derived sprites feel modern and premium without abandoning the retro sprite soul.
precedents.lessonForUs: Adopt a RESTRAINED version of this as the 'revamp' layer: real-time soft shadows, contact AO, gentle bloom, depth cue. It's mostly engine-side shader/trait work and instantly modernizes ALL existing art before any new unit is drawn.

precedents.name: Westwood Studios original C&C/Red Alert sprite production
precedents.whatTheyDid: Built units as 3D models, rendered them on an orthographic turntable to many facings, downscaled, and quantized to an indexed palette (then moved to real-time voxels in Tiberian Sun).
precedents.outcome: Produced perfectly rotationally-consistent 32-facing sprites at 1990s hardware budgets — the assets OpenRA runs on today.
precedents.lessonForUs: Reuse this exact pipeline in Blender. It is the only method that natively solves the 32-facing + animation + palette-remap requirement. OpenRA even kept a voxel/3D-model renderer, so part of this can run in real time.

precedents.name: Wargroove (Chucklefish) and Tooth and Tail (Pocketwatch)
precedents.whatTheyDid: Hand-authored HD pixel art with rigorous palette-swap faction recoloring (Wargroove) and ruthless unit-readability/silhouette discipline (Tooth and Tail: near-zero role overlap, instantly readable units).
precedents.outcome: Both celebrated for clarity; Tooth and Tail is a textbook example of 'you always know what a unit is and does.'
precedents.lessonForUs: Borrow the discipline, not the production method. Hand-pixeling a full modern roster is too labor-heavy and detail-capped — but enforce Tooth and Tail's silhouette/role-clarity gate and Wargroove's clean palette-swap team-color approach.

precedents.name: AI character-turnaround tooling (SDXL + LoRA + ControlNet/OpenPose, SpriteFlow et al.)
precedents.whatTheyDid: Attempt to generate multi-angle/multi-pose character sheets from one reference using seed locking, style LoRAs, and pose ControlNets.
precedents.outcome: Fast for one-offs, but the documented #1 failure is rotational inconsistency: silhouettes flip, outfits/palettes drift between angles, and re-rolls change the style — even with LoRA+ControlNet it's fragile, per-asset babysitting.
precedents.lessonForUs: Hard boundary: never use AI for the 32-facing in-world rotation set. DO use it for single-angle assets — concept art, build-icon cameos, faction iconography, loading/menu/hero art, and Codex illustrations — where it's genuinely the best tool.

feasibility.executiveSummary: OpenRA is HIGHLY suitable as a foundation for a contemporary retro-RTS. The engine already provides: (1) a working tech tree system that can model research dependencies mid-game; (2) support powers with charge mechanics for superweapons/special abilities; (3) multiple resource type support via a dictionary-based system; (4) veterancy via experience levels; (5) full procedural map generation; (6) an Encyclopedia widget for in-game codex; (7) a trait-based faction system with unit/building gating; (8) deterministic lock-step multiplayer suitable for complexity. Critical limitation: **player diplomacy relationships are set at game init and cannot be changed mid-game without engine modification** — this is the only major feature that needs new C# trait work. Lua scripting can expose any C# API you build. Estimated effort: 70% data-only mods (units/buildings/balance), 25% new C# trait traits (diplomacy system), 5% engine changes (if any).
keyFindings: DIPLOMACY/RELATIONSHIPS: Exists but STATIC — PlayerRelationship enum (Enemy/Neutral/Ally/None) is determined at game init via AlliedPlayersMask/EnemyPlayersMask in Player.cs. SetupPlayerMasks() in CreateMapPlayers.cs reads map-defined allies/enemies once. NO existing mechanism to change relationships mid-game; would require new C# trait that mutates these bitmasks and broadcasts state. Lua DiplomacyProperties only has IsAlliedWith() read method.

TECH TREE/PREREQUISITES: MATURE system. TechTree.cs in Traits/Player/ manages a prerequisite graph. ProvidesPrerequisite.cs grants prerequisites when actors exist (conditional). Buildable.cs gates production on prerequisites. System supports negated prerequisites (~! prefix for inverted checks). Can model arbitrary dependency chains. TechTree.HasPrerequisites() checks at runtime; changes are live as actors are added/removed. READY for research events.

SUPPORT POWERS: PRODUCTION-READY. SupportPowerInfo/SupportPower base classes. All existing powers inherit and override Activate(). Charge intervals in ticks, OneShot flag, Prerequisites array. Can add diplomacy-dependent powers (mod data). IonCannonPower et al. are examples. UI support in SupportPowersWidget. Can integrate with new research prerequisites.

ENCYCLOPEDIA WIDGET: EXISTS but MINIMAL. EncyclopediaInfo trait on actors supplies (Description, Category, Order, Scale, PreviewOwner). Logic in EncyclopediaLogic loads descriptions into UI. Already structured for expansion. Resource descriptions would need new trait or extension to encyclopia data model. Currently only covers units/buildings, not resource lore.

RESOURCES/ECONOMY: MULTI-TYPE CAPABLE. StoresResources.cs manages Dictionary<string,int> for per-type quantities within a single capacity. Harvester.cs specifies Resources array (Ore,Gems,etc). PlayerResources.cs has ResourceValues dict (monetary per unit-type). CAN support multiple distinct harvestable resources and per-resource values, but current engine only tracks one global player cash + one shared resource capacity. No per-resource cash tracking (fixable with new trait).

VETERANCY: FULL FEATURED. GainsExperience trait with conditions per level (frozen dictionary of XP%:ConditionName). Experience is synced [VerifySync]. Integrates with GivesExperience (kills grant XP) and transforms. Can gate unit upgrades via conditions. Ready to use.

MAP GENERATOR: PROCEDURAL GENERATION EXISTS. ClassicMapGenerator.cs (2 variants: Classic, Clear). Supports terrain, forests, resources, civilian buildings. Generates by seed; symmetric for multiplayer fairness. D2k has its own variant. NOT a runtime generator for single-player skirmish (would need game mode change), but editor tool. For skirmish random maps: would require integration with lobby/game launcher (architectural work).

FACTION SYSTEM: DATA-DRIVEN. FactionInfo trait on World actor lists Name/InternalName/Side/Selectable. BuildableInfo.ForceFaction gates specific units to factions. No 'subfaction' or 'variant' trait yet, but can use conditional traits or new ForceFaction variant. Currently units inherit faction from owner; EASY to add per-unit unique sprites/traits via trait conditions gated by faction.

DETERMINISM CONSTRAINT: ENFORCED. No float/random/DateTime in synced code. Fields marked [VerifySync] are XORed into per-frame sync hash. World coords use fixed-point (WPos/WDist/WAngle at 1024 units/cell). Diplomatic state changes MUST use [VerifySync] fields and synced orders. UI state strictly segregated (Sync.RunUnsynced guards it). Lua is unsynced but can issue orders. NEW diplomacy trait must mark all state [VerifySync].

LUA SCRIPTING REACH: 34 property groups exposed (Player, Production, Diplomacy, Health, etc). Can call C# trait methods via reflection. IsAlliedWith() readable. Can issue orders (OrderManager). Currently NO Lua-exposed method to change alliances — would need C# wrapper in ScriptPlayerProperties to issue a SetAlliance order. Low friction to add.

KEY FILES & EFFORT: (1) Diplomacy: NEW C# trait required (~200-300 LOC), emit synced SetAllianceOrder, mutate AlliedPlayersMask/EnemyPlayersMask, broadcast. Lua wrapper trivial. (2) Tech/Resources: 100% mod data. (3) Support powers: 100% mod data. (4) Map generation for skirmish: would need launcher/game mode work (medium effort). (5) Visual modernization: sprite art (the real cost: 32 facings × N units).
recommendations: PHASE 1 (Foundation): Implement dynamic diplomacy trait (SetAllianceOrderGenerator, SetAllianceOrder in Orders/, SetAllianceState trait on player actor) with Lua bindings. ~200 LOC C#, low risk. This unblocks all mid-game geopolitics.

PHASE 2 (Content): Define modern country factions with at least 1 unique unit + 1 unique building each. Use trait conditions and ForceFaction to gate variant sprites/abilities. Gearbox the existing tech tree for real-world tech progression (radar→satellite→AWACS etc). This is pure mod data.

PHASE 3 (Economy): Extend PlayerResources to track per-resource cash if needed (or just use resource points separate from cash). Create a ResourceMarket trait to simulate supply/demand. Current system supports it; just needs data.

PHASE 4 (Strategic Depth): Hook support powers into tech tree (prerequisites for nukes, airstrikes, etc.). Create event/victory conditions trait that rewards diplomatic plays (alliances, betrayals). Use existing MissionObjectives as model.

PHASE 5 (Skirmish): If random procedural maps are a must, integrate ClassicMapGenerator into game launcher (non-trivial but isolated). Otherwise ship hand-crafted balanced maps (faster to tune, better for esports).

AVOID EARLY: Sprite art (defer to last — art is the bottleneck, not engine). Full Civ-like culture/religion/era systems (violates 'real-time engaging' — keep it snappy). Floating-point camera (determinism forbids it; stick to 1024-unit grid).
risks: Diplomacy at game init only: Mitigation — implement SetAllianceOrder trait early (1-2 days C# work). No architecture blocker.
Sprite art cost: Each unit needs 32 PNG frames per faction variant. Feasible with in-game sprite editor (future) or outsourced art. Not an engine risk, but project risk.

Determinism fragility: Any float/random in new trait code causes desync. Mitigation — copy GainsExperience pattern (all fields [VerifySync], use WDist/CPos, no DateTime). Linter catches most violations (make check).

Encyclopedia data model: Current trait is minimal. Expanding it (resource descriptions, tech lore, faction history) requires new EncyclopediaInfo extensions. Not hard, but will sprawl YAML if done naively.
Multiple resource types: PlayerResources assumes one cash pool. Multi-resource cash (gold/oil/uranium each tradeable) needs new trait or refactor. Doable in ~200 LOC, but adds complexity.

Skirmish map generation: ClassicMapGenerator is editor-only. Wiring into game lobby/launcher requires knowing entry points (GameInfoScreen, *Ruleset mods). ~500 LOC, medium architectural knowledge needed.

Research pacing: Tech tree currently instant when prerequisites met. For Civ-like research 'progress bars', need new ResearchQueue trait similar to ProductionQueue. Medium effort (~300 LOC), but OpenRA doesn't have this model natively.

precedents.name: OpenRA's existing tech tree for prerequisites
precedents.whatTheyDid: TechTree trait watches for actors with ITechTreePrerequisite (e.g., ProvidesPrerequisite). When actor exists in world, its prerequisites unlock. Buildable checks HasPrerequisites() at build time.
precedents.outcome: Units/buildings gate automatically when prerequisites met. Supports negated checks (!nuke = disabled if nuke tech exists). No time/research queue; instant unlock.
precedents.lessonForUs: Same tech tree can model real-world tech progression (radar lab → grants 'radar' prerequisite → enables Radar Tower + Artillery). Just needs data definition. For Civ-like research TIME, add new ResearchQueue trait inspired by existing ProductionQueue.

precedents.name: Veterancy system (GainsExperience trait)
precedents.whatTheyDid: Tracks experience % synced. Grants conditions per level (e.g., 'veteran-lvl-1' at 50% XP, 'veteran-lvl-2' at 100%). Conditions trigger stat bonuses/weapons via existing conditional traits.
precedents.outcome: Units visibly level up in-game. Balanced via FrozenDictionary config. Ready for multiplayer.
precedents.lessonForUs: Same pattern for faction-specific unit variants: gate armor/speed/firepower via conditions tied to faction. Faction traits can grant starting conditions or unlock via tech tree.

precedents.name: Support powers with prerequisites
precedents.whatTheyDid: SupportPowerInfo.Prerequisites array gates power availability. When prerequisite missing, power is disabled. UI grays out icon.
precedents.outcome: Nuclear weapons can require 'nuke-silo' prerequisite. Power charges then fires. Visuals tied to charge state.
precedents.lessonForUs: Superweapons naturally slot into a tech tree. Add support-power-specific research (e.g., 'ion-cannon' grants ability to build Ion Cannon power). No new code needed, just YAML data.

precedents.name: Player actor traits for diplomacy
precedents.whatTheyDid: DiplomacyProperties (Lua) reads Player.IsAlliedWith() at runtime. PlayerRelationship enum used throughout (AutoTarget, Mine, etc.).
precedents.outcome: Game logic queries 'is player A allied with player B' constantly. Relationship static for match duration.
precedents.lessonForUs: Betrayal/alliance changes need to mutate AlliedPlayersMask/EnemyPlayersMask and notify all traits via INotifyPlayerRelationshipChange (new interface). Similar to existing INotifyOwnerChanged pattern. Moderate refactor of 1-2 days.

precedents.name: Faction-specific unit gating (ForceFaction)
precedents.whatTheyDid: Buildable.ForceFaction overrides producing faction's faction. Allows USA-only Rangers vs GDI-only Militants in same Tiberian Dawn ruleset.
precedents.outcome: Each faction has unique units without duplication. Production queue filters by faction at build time.
precedents.lessonForUs: For modern RTS, define ~8 countries as factions. Each has ForceFaction units (e.g., 'USA/USAF: F-22 Raptor', 'Russia/RKZ: MiG-31'). Add unique buildings same way. Faction traits (speed/armor bonuses) applied via conditions.

precedents.name: Resource harvesting with multiple types (Harvester/StoresResources)
precedents.whatTheyDid: Harvester.Resources array lists Ore,Gems etc. StoresResources holds Dictionary<ResourceType,Amount>. ResourceValues dict in PlayerResources prices each type.
precedents.outcome: Harvesters collect multiple resource types. Refinery stores and unloads proportionally. Player cash increases per resource-type value.
precedents.lessonForUs: Base system works. For strategic resources (iron only from mines, oil from derricks), just define different resource types and place them on map via editor. Current engine supports it.

## DETAILED FEASIBILITY ANALYSIS

### (1) Player Diplomacy / Relationships / Stances

**Status:** PARTIAL — relationships exist but are STATIC at game init.

**What Exists:**
- `PlayerRelationship` enum in `/Users/ashishnaik/Projects/openra/OpenRA.Game/Traits/TraitsInterfaces.cs:65` (Enemy, Neutral, Ally, None as flags).
- Each `Player` has `AlliedPlayersMask` and `EnemyPlayersMask` as `LongBitSet<PlayerBitMask>`.
- `Player.RelationshipWith(other)` method queries these bitmasks in real-time.
- Relationships initialized in `CreateMapPlayers.SetupPlayerMasks()` (`OpenRA.Mods.Common/Traits/World/CreateMapPlayers.cs:142`), reading map-defined Allies/Enemies lists and Team assignments.
- Lua has `DiplomacyProperties.IsAlliedWith(player)` for read-only queries.

**What's Missing:**
- NO trait or order mechanism to change relationships mid-game.
- AlliedPlayersMask and EnemyPlayersMask are public fields but never mutated after init.
- No `SetAllianceOrder`, no `INotifyPlayerRelationshipChange` interface, no Lua method to change alliance.

**Effort to Add:**
- NEW C# trait `DynamicAlliance` or extend player actor: ~250 LOC.
  - Create `SetAllianceOrder` in `OpenRA.Game/Orders/` (~50 LOC).
  - Order processor in new trait mutates AlliedPlayersMask/EnemyPlayersMask, marks [VerifySync].
  - Broadcast state change via new interface `INotifyPlayerRelationshipChanged` (similar to `INotifyOwnerChanged`).
  - Add Lua wrapper in `ScriptPlayerProperties` (~30 LOC).
- Risk: MEDIUM. Determinism-critical (all state must be synced). Must audit all code that caches relationship checks.
- Timeline: 1–2 days.

**Files Involved:**
- `/Users/ashishnaik/Projects/openra/OpenRA.Game/Player.cs` (add setter/interface call)
- `/Users/ashishnaik/Projects/openra/OpenRA.Game/Orders/UnitOrders.cs` (or new file for order processor)
- `/Users/ashishnaik/Projects/openra/OpenRA.Mods.Common/Traits/Player/TechTree.cs` (consider adding prerequisite for alliances, e.g., 'diplomatic-office' grants ability to negotiate)
- `/Users/ashishnaik/Projects/openra/OpenRA.Mods.Common/Scripting/Properties/DiplomacyProperties.cs` (add method).

---

### (2) Tech Tree / Research System

**Status:** EXISTS & MATURE. Prerequisite graph fully implemented.

**What Exists:**
- `TechTree` trait on player actor (`OpenRA.Mods.Common/Traits/Player/TechTree.cs`). Manages a set of "watchers" (prerequisites and build limits).
- `ProvidesPrerequisite` trait on actors (`OpenRA.Mods.Common/Traits/Player/ProvidesPrerequisite.cs`). When placed in world, grants a prerequisite (e.g., actor 'RadarDome' grants 'radar' prerequisite).
- `Buildable` trait (`OpenRA.Mods.Common/Traits/Buildable.cs`). Prerequisites field is an array of strings. Can be prefixed with `!` (inverted) or `~` (hidden if missing).
- TechTree.HasPrerequisites() is a live runtime check. As actors are added/destroyed, prerequisites granted/revoked dynamically.
- Can model chains: e.g., 'infantry-barracks' provides 'infantry', which enables 'heavy-infantry-upgrade', which enables upgraded infantry in barracks.

**Real-World Example:**
```yaml
RadarDome:
  Buildable:
    Prerequisites: advanced-construction  # requires Conyard upgrade
  ProvidesPrerequisite:
    Prerequisite: radar
    RequiresPrerequisites: construction    # only grants if you have Conyard
---
ArmoredPersonnelCarrier:
  Buildable:
    Prerequisites: heavy-unit-factory, radar  # needs heavy factory AND radar
```

**No Time/Progress Bar:**
- Buildable.BuildDuration is in frames, but it's production queue time (how long to build a single unit), NOT tech research time.
- If you need "spend 5 min researching Heavy Armor before Heavy Tank is available," you'd need a new trait `ResearchQueue` (similar to `ProductionQueue` but for tech). Not in current engine.

**Effort to Add Time-Based Research:**
- Create `ResearchQueueInfo` + `ResearchQueue` trait (~300 LOC) on player, inspired by `OpenRA.Mods.Common/Traits/Player/ProductionQueue.cs`.
- Add `ResearchProgress` orders and UI widget.
- Integrate with TechTree: when ResearchQueue completes "Heavy Armor" tech, call TechTree.Update().
- Timeline: 2–3 days.

**For This Project (Contemporary RTS):**
- **Recommendation:** Use instant tech tree first (unlock when building exists), then add time-based research if needed. Most balance is fine with instant unlock. If you want "researching satellite" → grants vision upgrade, instant is snappy (real-time friendly).

### (9) Determinism & Sync Constraints

**Status:** ENFORCED. Well-documented, tooling in place.

**Key Rules:**
1. **No float/double** in synced code. Use fixed-point types: `WDist` (1024 units = 1 cell), `WPos` (world position), `WAngle` (0–1023 = 0–360°), `CPos/CVec` (cell coords).
2. **No Random/DateTime** except in unsynced (UI) code. Use `MersenneTwister` for seeded RNG.
3. **All mutable sync state** must be marked `[VerifySync]` attribute. Sync.cs XORs these fields into per-frame hash.
4. All synced code is in `world.Tick()` and Activities. UI/rendering runs in `TickRender()` (unsynced).
5. **Orders** are the only cross-network communication. Everything else is determined by inputs.

**Linter Enforcement:**
- `make check` runs `CheckSyncAnnotations` lint rule, catches common mistakes (float in [VerifySync], non-int fields).
- Desync detected → SyncHash mismatch → game pauses, logged.

**For Diplomacy Trait:**
- All relationship state must be `[VerifySync]`.
- SetAllianceOrder must be synced (issued by all clients for the same player).
- Any trait that caches alliance checks must invalidate cache when order processes.

**For Procedural Map Gen:**
- Use game's `MersenneTwister` (seeded from lobby), not `Random`.
- All generation is deterministic per seed.

**Effort to Respect Constraints:**

## BIGGEST CHALLENGE: SPRITE ART

Each unit needs **32 facing directions** in PNG format (~64×64 px each). For a contemporary RTS with 8 countries × 10 unit types each = 80 unique units × 32 facings = **2,560 sprite sheets**. This is the **real cost ceiling**, not the engine.

**Mitigation:**
1. Use existing OpenRA sprites (Red Alert, Tiberian Dawn) and modify via editor/tools.
2. Commission art from pixel-art studios ($50–200 per unit type).
3. Use low-poly 3D + real-time sprite render (high effort, but future-proof).

The engine handles art via data-driven Rendering traits; no engine changes needed.

design.workingTitle: THEATER — Contemporary Command (working title; internal codename "Bleed-Modern")
design.visionStatement: THEATER is Red Alert's fast, readable RTS heartbeat fused with Rise of Nations' strategic systems and Company of Heroes' decision-density — a contemporary-military total conversion of OpenRA where 12 lightly-fictionalized real-world blocs fight 20-40 minute matches that feel like Stellaris envelops you in complexity, minus the slowness. You still harvest, build, and counter-compose under fog of war, but the shallow "mass the best unit and A-move" loop is structurally dead: territory IS the economy, strategic deposits gate your high-tech doctrine, supply convoys are cuttable, live diplomacy with bribable neutral city-states gives even a 1v1 a third party to fight over, and modern layered air-defense turns "defense" into an active cost-exchange gamble rather than a turtle wall. Every system cross-couples (economy gates research, research reshapes diplomacy leverage, diplomacy reshapes the map you fight over) so depth emerges from a few interacting rules, not many parallel meters. The look is "HD-Pixel diorama" — Blender-rendered clean 32-facing sprites that de-blur the classics while keeping chunky readable retro silhouettes, with a restrained modern post layer (soft shadows, gentle bloom) and an Encyclopedia/Codex that teaches the real critical-minerals and real military tech behind every unit at the moment it becomes relevant.
designPillars: DECISION DENSITY, NOT MANAGEMENT LOAD (Sid Meier's filter as an engineering constraint). Every system must add ~1 genuinely interesting non-dominated choice per 10-20 seconds and near-zero forced busywork. If the optimal play is always the same, the system is decoration and gets cut or redesigned — applied per faction, per unit, per building. This is the explicit answer to 'add diplomacy/research/economy ≠ fun.'

FEW SYSTEMS THAT CROSS-COUPLE (the Rise of Nations / anti-Stellaris rule). Depth comes from a small number of systems feeding each other (economy gates research, research unlocks diplomacy leverage, diplomacy reshapes contested map), never from many parallel auto-optimized meters. Prefer combinatorial depth from interaction over additive complexity from multiplication.

TERRITORY IS THE GAME (the Company of Heroes lesson). The strategic map is the economy, the tech-access layer, and the diplomacy object simultaneously. Harvester micro is minimized; holding/cutting connected ground and contested deposits is where strategy lives — which also structurally kills the deathball by rewarding spread and forward presence.

ASYMMETRY BY STRATEGIC USE, NOT STAT TIERS (the StarCraft 2 / real-country answer). The 12 blocs share a base set but differ by a single signature mechanic + one unique unit + one unique building, each occupying a distinct point on the cost/quality, offense/defense, and information axes. Every strength is also an exploitable seam. Matchups, not raw numbers, generate the interesting decisions.

PROGRESSIVE DISCLOSURE KEEPS IT FAST (the flow-channel rule). The core RTS loop is fun BEFORE any advanced system unlocks. Research/diplomacy/strategic-resources reveal their UI in layers as the match progresses, and the Codex doubles as a just-in-time tutorial, so minute-one is never an overwhelming 4X system-dump.
coreLoops: ECONOMIC (territory-gated, two-tier): Credits flow from two abundant open-field resources (Petroleum + Iron) in the classic harvest-under-threat loop — the bread-and-butter economy a new player relies on alone. Layered on top: a small number of contested CENTRAL strategic DEPOSITS (Rare Earths / Uranium / Lithium) that must be physically held and TRUCKED home via cuttable supply convoys. Holding ground = income AND tech access; cutting a convoy chokes the enemy's high-tech production without touching their base.

PRODUCTION + RESEARCH (three-layer, see systems.research): build base/power/units as classic OpenRA, but teching is a shared-pool gamble (research draws the SAME credits as units) across 3 Era gates, 1 irreversible Doctrine fork, and a few mutually-exclusive Era upgrade forks. 'Tech up now and go army-light, or stay this era and out-mass' is the heartbeat.

COMBAT (composition + counters, modern-flavored): rock-paper-scissors at the COMPOSITION level with hard counters and real top-unit vulnerabilities, so a pure top-tier stack is cost-inefficient and must be screened. Scouting the enemy economy = scouting their tech (you can see they seized a Rare-Earth deposit and are teching to drones). Positioning and combined arms, not APM, are the skill axis.

ACTIVE DEFENSE (cost-exchange, see systems.defense): a layered air-defense ladder where interception is a finite-ammo, success-CHANCE, per-shot-cost mechanic. The defender makes 2-4 live decisions during an assault (allocate interceptors, fire counter-battery, pop a jam burst, reposition mobile SHORAD) — defense as verbs, not autopilot.

DIPLOMACY + CITY-STATES (live, fast, see systems.diplomacy): a one-click radial of 7 templated, time-boxed, binding agreements plus bribable neutral minor factions on every map. Race the opponent for the loyalty of 1-3 minors; betrayal is allowed, telegraphed, and priced. This is the loop that makes the strategic layer live even in 1v1 and skirmish-vs-AI.

SUPPORT-POWER / SUPERWEAPON (doctrine payoff): superweapons are earned via sustained territory + strategic-resource upkeep (nuke gated by Uranium, drone swarm by Rare Earth, rail/DEW by Lithium), telegraphed per OpenRA convention. They punctuate and break stalemates rather than being a bare timer.
antiTankSpam: TERRITORY IS THE ECONOMY (CoH model): income and high-tech access both come from holding connected map sectors and contested central deposits, not from a base-bound harvester loop. Massing one unit and A-moving abandons the map; spreading to hold ground beats blobbing. This single mechanic simultaneously removes harvester micro, forces map-wide decisions, and discourages the deathball.

SUPPLY-LINE / CONVOY CUTTING: strategic resources must be trucked from deposit to a Stockpile building (reskinned harvester+refinery loop). Convoys are raidable, so you can choke an enemy's drone/nuke/DEW production by hitting his logistics rather than his army — economic warfare as a real attack vector, nearly free in art.

HARD COUNTERS WITH REAL TOP-UNIT VULNERABILITIES: every signature unit ships an explicit strong-vs / weak-vs and a genuine seam (USA's networked buff collapses if its C2 node is sniped; the German Leopard dies to top-attack/flanking; Iran's swarm folds to area/splash AA; the theater SAM has a point-blank dead zone and MUST be screened by SHORAD). A pure top-tier stack is strictly cost-inefficient vs a screened mixed force, so armies stay compositions.

SATURATION VALVE (cost-exchange defense): interceptors are finite-ammo and cost credits per shot, so any fixed defense is beatable by out-producing its magazine (the real Shahed-vs-Patriot doctrine). Magazines are visible (pips) so a drained battery is an exploitable opening — defense can never become an unbreakable turtle.

RESEARCH AS OPPORTUNITY COST, NOT BACKGROUND PROGRESS: teching draws the SAME credit pool (and build slot) as units, and high-tech doctrines carry ongoing strategic-resource UPKEEP that drains while active. 'I unlocked drones' becomes the live tension 'can I keep them fed and defended?' — so spamming tier-1 is never the free dominant line.

FOOD/WATER UPKEEP CAP (soft population meter, reuses Power pattern): a bigger army demands more territory to sustain it; exceeding the cap slows production/healing. Adds expansion tension with zero micromanagement — a passive bar, not a chore.

DECISION-DENSITY METRICS AS SHIP GATES: track how often the same opening/composition wins (dominant-strategy alarm), idle/menu-staring time (analysis-paralysis alarm), and late-game busywork APM (tedium alarm). A system ships only if it passes the no-dominant-strategy lens in playtest, not on enthusiasm.
design.pacingModel: Target a 20-40 minute match shaped as a single real-time layer (NO Total-War two-layer trap, NO Stellaris pause-to-think dependency). The pacing spine is 3 ERA advancements (Present Day -> Networked/EW -> Autonomous/drone-swarm -> Near-Future/hypersonic+DEW), each a big paid timed gate that raises the ceiling and re-opens the rock-paper-scissors — the AoE 'power spike' beat, kept to 4 tiers so snowball stays bounded. 'Stellaris depth at RTS speed' is delivered three ways, none of which slow the clock: (1) DEPTH-FROM-INTERACTION — three cross-coupled systems (territory-economy, doctrine-research, diplomacy-over-minors) produce combinatorial possibility-space from few rules, so the game feels enveloping without adding per-second load; (2) TENSION INSTEAD OF LENGTH (Northgard/They-Are-Billions) — escalating strategic-resource upkeep, supply pressure, and scripted Lua events force high-stakes commit/expand/turtle timing decisions rather than menu depth; (3) AUTOMATE-THE-TEDIUM — anything that scales with empire size and has an obviously-correct answer (resource hauling, repeat production) is automatable penalty-free so attention stays on interesting decisions. Hard rule: every strategic action must resolve as 'pay X, wait Y (seconds-to-low-minutes), now Z is visibly different on the map' — if it can't be said that way it's too grand-strategy and gets cut. Anti-stalemate valves keep it moving: all diplomatic pacts are time-boxed and decay (permanent peace impossible), defenses are saturation-vulnerable and upkeep-hungry, and map resources are spread so sitting is always worse than expanding. Decision-density ceiling is enforced as a budget: at most ~5 actionable strategic choices on screen at once (era-up button + unlocked doctrine perks + the 1-2 open upgrade forks for what you're building); the full tree lives read-only in the Codex.

systems.diplomacy: LIVE, FAST, BINDING (extend the engine's 3-state mask, don't replace it). Keep Ally/Enemy/Neutral as the ground truth the sim reads (AutoTarget, Locomotor, shroud all key off the existing AlliedPlayersMask/EnemyPlayersMask in Player.cs); layer a DiplomacyManager trait that holds per-pair Agreement records (type + integer expiry tick + flags) and, on change, recomputes the masks via a SYNCED order (the engine currently sets masks once at game-init via CreateMapPlayers.SetupPlayerMasks and never mutates them — this is the only genuinely new C# of the diplomacy feature, ~250 LOC). FIXED MENU OF 7 templated agreements (no free-text negotiation): Ceasefire, NAP, Alliance (shared vision + WC3-style shared CONTROL permission flag with NO ownership transfer + see partner production), Defensive Pact (anti-gang: auto-war if partner attacked), Trade Route (passive credits via a physical RAIDABLE convoy), Vision Share, Vassal/Protectorate (anti-elimination comeback mechanic). KEYSTONE: 1-3 neutral bribable MINOR FACTIONS / city-states on every map (a militia, an oil baron, a tech lab) implemented as ProximityCapturable + a MinorFaction trait holding an integer loyalty-per-player; highest loyalty allies the minor, an enemy can out-bid or storm it. This is what makes diplomacy LIVE in 1v1 and skirmish-vs-AI — you race the opponent for the minors. AI/minor acceptance uses a TRANSPARENT integer opinion score (Sins/Stellaris model) itemized on hover; all integer, event-driven, no float/Random (lockstep-safe). UI is a one-click radial on player/minor portraits + dismissable accept/decline toasts with countdown rings (reuse ProductionPaletteWidget grid + support-power timer ring). BETRAYAL is the fun engine: always allowed via the same radial, but telegraphed to the victim with a ~3-5s grace window before your units may fire, and priced via a persistent Trust stat minors and AI remember. Anti-stalemate: all pacts time-boxed and decaying, max 1-2 alliances per player, war-restlessness on long peace. Phased art-free first: order+enum+timers+opinion playable/testable via extended Lua DiplomacyProperties before any UI; gate behind a 'Diplomacy: On/Off' lobby option so ranked 1v1 can disable it.
systems.research: THREE LAYERS, NOT ONE TREE (built on existing prerequisite + condition + support-power traits + ONE new ResearchQueue trait modeled on ProductionQueue, integer cost/tick, [Sync]). LAYER 1 ERAS: 3 advancements (Present Day -> Networked/EW -> Autonomous -> Near-Future) at a single R&D/Command HQ, each costing significant credits AND production time and gated behind a built structure; advancing RAISES THE CEILING (unlocks next units + next upgrade fork) rather than a flat buff, preserving the tech-up-vs-spend gamble. Kept to 3 (not Empire Earth's 15) to bound snowball. LAYER 2 DOCTRINE: one IRREVERSIBLE Company-of-Heroes-style fork into Economy / Military / Defense / Diplomacy-Intel, slowly unlocking 3-5 perks over the match; this is each country's identity and the home for its unique unit+building, and what makes diplomacy/EW/defense first-class axes. Show all four up front (the one big legible choice), reveal perks progressively. LAYER 3 ERA UPGRADES: per era, ~2-4 BIG mutually-exclusive 'pick N of M' forks that change HOW a unit fights (Grey Goo / Universe-at-War standard), never an invisible +1: Drone Swarm vs Hypersonic Strike vs Directed-Energy point-defense vs Cyber/EW package — and that counter-triangle (swarm beats armor, lasers beat swarm, cyber beats networked) is itself the strategic game. HARD RULE enforced in lint/review: any upgrade everyone always buys in the same order is folded into the (free, automatic) era unlock or rebuilt as a fork — no StarCraft-style mandatory stat taxes. Tech competes with spend (same credit pool + build slot). At most ~5 live research choices on screen; full future tree lives in the read-only Codex.
systems.economyAndResources: THREE-PILLAR MODEL: 1 fluid currency + 3 strategic stockpiles + 2 soft meters + a supply-line overlay — the sweet spot between StarCraft's 2 resources and Civ's spreadsheet (and the engine cleanly supports only ~7 tile resource indices anyway). (1) CREDITS, fed by two ABUNDANT open-field resources, Petroleum + Iron, both mapping to the single PlayerResources cash pool via ResourceValues exactly like Ore/Gems today — zero new systems, the classic harvest-under-threat loop survives intact. (2) THREE SCARCE STRATEGIC STOCKPILES — Rare Earths / Uranium / Lithium — held as SEPARATE integer counters (a thin clone of PlayerResources), fed by a few contested central DEPOSIT tiles, NOT spent like cash but acting as PREREQUISITE + slow-UPKEEP gates on three distinct top-tier doctrines (drones/EW, nuclear, batteries/DEW) via a generalized GrantConditionOnPlayerResources. This is where territory becomes strategy: you can win on credits with a conventional army but CANNOT field the high-tech edge without physically holding the deposit, and upkeep means losing it visibly degrades your edge over time. (3) FOOD/WATER, a soft population/upkeep meter reusing the PowerManager pattern verbatim (raise cap with farms/desal, exceed it = slowed production/healing). (4) SUPPLY LINES: stockpiles are TRUCKED deposit->Stockpile via the reskinned harvester+refinery+dock loop; cut the convoy and choke enemy high-tech without touching their base. Player watches 1 number constantly + 3 occasionally + 2 passive bars — under the working-memory ceiling. Silicon/Titanium/Copper/Cobalt/Phosphate are NOT counters; they live in the CODEX as building/unit lore (educate-via-codex-breadth, gate-via-mechanic-narrowness). Factions differ by resource EFFICIENCY/ACCESS, not set (China: Rare-Earth/Titanium discounts; Russia: Uranium/aerospace; USA/EU: cheap-conventional-but-import-dependent), so the same map plays differently per country. All integer, deterministic, lockstep-safe. Ship MVP first: Credits + exactly ONE stockpile (Rare Earths gating a drone/EW doctrine) to prove the 'territory = tech access' loop before adding Uranium/Lithium.
systems.defense: LAYERED, TIERED, ACTIVE COST-EXCHANGE — defense buys TIME and force-economy, never invulnerability (the load-bearing real-world fact: a $35K drone soaking a $4.2M interceptor is a 120:1 loss, so defense is an economic gamble). FOUR PILLARS: (1) 3-TIER AIR-DEFENSE LADDER with band-locked efficiency — Gun SHORAD (cheap, hitscan, infinite ammo, kills aircraft/drones/cheap rockets, the only AD allowed to be weakly mobile) -> C-RAM/Iron-Dome (medium, FINITE AmmoPool magazine, chance-to-intercept rockets/artillery/missiles/drones, the workhorse) -> Theater SAM (expensive, long range, MINIMUM-RANGE DEAD ZONE so it MUST be screened, tiny costly magazine, the only answer to ballistic/superweapon threats); using a high tier on a low threat is a deliberate WASTE. (2) INTERCEPTION AS SUCCESS-CHANCE + AMMO + PER-SHOT COST — a new PointDefense trait extending the existing JamsMissiles chance pattern: each incoming projectile in range rolls intercept chance (via SYNCED world RNG / MersenneTwister, never System.Random), consumes one round, deducts credits; magazines visible as pips so a drained battery is exploitable; saturation/swarm is the built-in anti-turtle valve. (3) INFORMATION/EW LAYER as a separate, FRAGILE, high-value building class (Early-Warning Radar that buffs nearby AD and whose death degrades the whole net = real SEAD; Jammer that cuts enemy accuracy/homing; cheap Anti-Drone RF; Counter-Battery Radar that paints enemy artillery) — wins by DENIAL not kills, and invites raids creating tempo instead of turtling. (4) POSITIONAL FORTIFICATION that shapes WHERE fights happen, not walls that end them (garrison bunkers flushable by flame/EMP, trenches, mine-fields cleared by detectors, hardpoints you slot AA/AT/anti-infantry modules into, decoys/camo for bluffing). ANTI-STALEMATE CHECKLIST as a ship gate per defense: priced below equivalent army value, saturation-beatable, costs ongoing power/upkeep/restock, strongest form immobile, and expanding beats sitting. Mostly YAML composition of existing traits; modest new C# (PointDefense, CounterBattery). MVP: ship the EW/information + interception layer first (auras + reskinned statics, cheap art) before expensive animated turret sprites.

design.countryModel: 12 lightly-fictionalized real-world BLOCS (not raw national flags — 'The Federation'=USA-flavored, 'Northern Union'=Russia-flavored, etc.) on OpenRA's proven sub-faction template: each bloc = a distinct PLAYSTYLE expressed through ONE signature mechanic + ONE unique UNIT + ONE unique BUILDING + a strategic NICHE, balanced by ROLE not power tier. Grounded in real force structure: USA=networked air/naval power-projection (Stealth Strike Fighter 'Specter' + Joint Command Network C2 node whose aura buffs the whole army but collapses if sniped); China=mass+A2/AD missile-umbrella+drones (Area-Denial Missile Battery + Integrated Defense Grid dome); Russia=armor+EW+massed artillery (EW Command Tank 'Bastion' that jams enemy targeting + Artillery Fire-Direction Center); Germany=engineering/armor durability (durable self-repairing MBT 'Loewe' + Field Engineering Depot); France=expeditionary precision+deterrent (multirole swap-loadout jet + Strategic Deterrence Silo that SLOWS enemy super-power charge, framed as deterrence not city-buster); UK=naval/expeditionary/intel (cloaked SAS recon team + Maritime Operations Centre that reveals enemy support-power launches); Israel=active-protection+interception+precision (APS tank that intercepts the first missile + Iron-Dome Interception Dome that hard-counters artillery/missile/super-weapons); India=layered shielded arsenal+numbers (supersonic BrahMos cruise launcher under an S-400/Akash air-defense umbrella); Japan=naval Aegis missile-defense+robotics (Aegis BMD destroyer + Autonomous Systems Lab spawning robot escorts); South Korea=sensor-to-shooter C4I+artillery (networked K9 howitzer that fires faster when spotted + C4I Fusion Center); Turkey=cheap attritable drones+EW (mass Bayraktar-style UCAV + Drone Command & EW Post); Iran=asymmetric swarm+denial (dirt-cheap Shahed loitering-munition salvos + dispersed redundant 'mosaic' production hard to decapitate). BALANCING PHILOSOPHY (asymmetric-but-fair, four rules): (1) every faction has a PAIRED strength+weakness — its strength is the seam an opponent attacks; (2) signature units are SIDEGRADES with explicit strong-vs/weak-vs hard counters, never stat-superior reskins; (3) power-budget parity via cost/build-limit/fragile-enabler-building (a strong unique unit costs more or has a killable enabler); (4) the unique BUILDING is an ENABLER that changes HOW you play, not a flat economy boost. Factions span a design space (cost/quality axis: USA/Japan elite-expensive <-> Iran/Turkey cheap-expendable; offense/defense axis: Korea/USA proactive <-> Israel/Japan/China reactive-denial; information axis: UK/USA/Korea see-first <-> Russia/Iran deny-information) and a closed counter-loop (missiles/drones -> hard-countered by interception -> beaten by kinetic armor + saturation -> out-ranged by artillery -> die to air/recon raids -> die to air-defense domes). SENSITIVITY STANCE: fictional callsigns over real designations; all factions framed as defensive DOCTRINES not aggressors with no reference to real wars/atrocities/leaders/insignia; nuclear/strategic weapons abstracted as telegraphed deterrence-flavored powers; Codex entries teach real ENGINEERING/doctrine facts framed educationally, never propaganda; ship a settings toggle for fully-abstract sci-fi-bloc names ('flavor-on' or 'flavor-neutral') for sensitive markets/esports. ART DISCIPLINE (the real ceiling): one SHARED modern-military base set reused by all blocs via palette/skin swap; each faction gets ONLY its one signature unit as bespoke 32-facing art (12 hero sprites) + one signature building. SCOPING: launch with 6 cleanest anchors (USA/Russia/China/Israel/Turkey/Korea spanning the whole space) and prove balance before the phase-2 six (France/UK/Germany/Japan/India/Iran).
design.visualDirection: 'HD-Pixel diorama' — sits between the C&C Remastered / They-Are-Billions / AoE-Definitive-Edition pole (clean 3D-rendered-to-2D sprites = the de-blur) and a RESTRAINED Octopath HD-2D post layer (= the 'modern revamp'). GOVERNING RULE from the C&C Remaster postmortem: at fixed top-down RTS zoom, MORE realism reads WORSE, so the target is clean-and-bold-not-photoreal — silhouette-first, chunky exaggerated forms, detail spent on the outline and faction color, every unit ID-able as a flat black silhouette at 100% zoom. PIPELINE IS HYBRID and non-negotiable: Blender 3D-model -> orthographic turntable render (camera steps 360/32 = 11.25deg at OpenRA's classic ~30-35deg pitch) -> downscale -> indexed-palette = rotationally PERFECT 32 facings by construction (exactly how Westwood and the Remaster did it). AI image generation is structurally BAD at rotational consistency (silhouette flips, palette drift across angles is its documented #1 failure) so it is FORBIDDEN for the in-world rotation set, but is the RIGHT tool for everything single-angle: concept/silhouette exploration, sidebar build-icon cameos, faction iconography, loading/menu/hero art, and especially the Codex plates. Team color is a HARD constraint designed in from frame one: author each unit's team-color region as a flat unlit remap ramp, render a beauty pass + a remap-mask pass, quantize onto OpenRA's reserved PlayerColorRemap indices. THE ENGINE ALREADY SHIPS THE PLUMBING (this is an art/asset effort, not an engine rewrite): a real-time voxel/3D-model renderer with data-driven lighting (RenderVoxels.cs LightPitch/LightYaw/Ambient/Diffuse, used by the TS mod), a non-palette RGBA PNG sprite path (PngSheetLoader.cs), and a shipping TiberianDawnHD mod proving runtime classic/HD asset toggling. The 'revamp' layer is mostly engine-side shader/trait work that upgrades ALL existing art at once before a single new unit is drawn: real-time soft drop shadows, base-contact ambient occlusion, restrained bloom on muzzle flash/energy/explosions, gentle depth/atmosphere cue. Render new sprites at 2-4x classic footprint for the de-blur. Roll out as a VERTICAL SLICE first (one bloc ~6 units + 4 buildings + matching terrain, fully through Blender->sprite->team-color->in-engine, shipped beside classic via the runtime toggle) and get readability sign-off at real combat zoom BEFORE scaling; convert by complete faction+terrain sets to avoid mixed-asset incoherence.
design.uiDirection: 'Clean military HUD' that modernizes without breaking muscle memory: flatter panels, a tightened grid, crisp vector/SDF UI icons, 1-2 faction accent colors, a legible modern sans for data with a retro display face reserved for headers — but KEEP the command-sidebar layout intact (the ladder player's reflexes are sacred). Progressive disclosure is the organizing principle: minute-one shows only the core RTS HUD; the research/era-up button, unlocked doctrine perks, the diplomacy radial, and the strategic-resource counters reveal themselves as the match unlocks them, so the full 4X surface is never dumped at once (the documented onboarding-cliff killer for hybrids). New UI surfaces, each reusing existing engine chrome: (1) DIPLOMACY — a one-click radial on enemy/neutral/minor portraits showing only LEGAL agreement transitions as production-style icons, plus dismissable accept/decline toasts with support-power-style countdown rings, and itemized opinion-on-hover for AI/minors; (2) RESEARCH — at most ~5 live choices (era-up + doctrine perks + 1-2 open upgrade forks), the rest read-only in the Codex; (3) DEFENSE — visible interceptor-magazine PIPS, range/detection RINGS with the theater-SAM dead zone shown, and target-priority toggles, so coverage gaps are legible and patchable; (4) ECONOMY — one prominent Credits number, three small strategic-stockpile counters surfaced only once you control a deposit, and two passive Power and Food/Water bars. THE CODEX (the existing Encyclopedia widget at EncyclopediaLogic.cs + mods/*/chrome/encyclopedia.yaml, extended) is both the strategic-depth reference and a just-in-time teacher: left nav tree (Resources / Units / Buildings / Factions / Doctrines), a big AI-generated hero plate per entry (the single-angle case where AI excels), a structured stat block, and cross-links. It surfaces a resource's real-world role (silicon/Taiwan, cobalt/DRC, rare-earths/China) and a unit's real military basis DIEGETICALLY — the card pops the first time you mine that deposit or unlock a unit that needs it — turning real lore into onboarding for the new systems rather than required homework. Strictly optional and asynchronous; never gates a decision.
openDesignQuestions: TIME-BOXED PACT TUNING is load-bearing and unproven: if alliances/NAPs are too cheap, long, or uncapped, FFA collapses into one frozen mega-bloc (the opposite of fast); too short and diplomacy is noise. The exact durations, alliance caps (1-2?), and war-restlessness curve can only be found in playtest — and they entangle with economy/tech balance since a strong Trade Route or tech-lab minor could dominate.

ERA-UP TIMING is the single most balance-sensitive number: too slow/expensive and the dominant strategy becomes 'never tech, mass tier-1' and a rush kills the teching player while army-light; too cheap and the snowball/runaway-leader problem (a player one era ahead being near-unbeatable) makes 1v1 unfun. Needs cross-era hard counters (a Present-Day MANPADS ambush still killing a Near-Future asset) and careful first-push survivability tuning.

DOCTRINE BALANCE / 'one best doctrine' trap: the irreversible Economy/Military/Defense/Diplomacy fork is only fun if all four are viable per faction. If Military always wins, the choice collapses to a non-decision — and this is where most of the tuning effort and per-faction balance cost will land. Is a hard counter-relationship between doctrines needed, or just numeric parity?

HOW MANY STRATEGIC STOCKPILES to actually ship: the design caps at 3 (Rare Earths/Uranium/Lithium) and the MVP ships 1, but is even 3 too much cognitive load in real-time combat, or could a 4th (e.g. a separate drone vs nuke vs DEW gate) add meaningful asymmetry without tipping into spreadsheet tedium? The working-memory ceiling is a hypothesis to validate.

MINOR-FACTION REWARDS vs ART CEILING: the most exciting minor rewards (a free batch of a unique unit) depend on sprite art that may not exist at launch. Do phase-1 minors give only art-free payloads (credits, income %, tech unlock, vision), and how much does that blunt the 'race for the minors' fantasy that makes 1v1 diplomacy live?

EMP / POWER-GRID SINGLE POINT OF FAILURE: tying the whole AD/EW net to power makes an EMP raid able to swing defense from oppressive to useless in one move — exciting, but potentially a coin-flip. How much graceful degradation / battery-backed core defense is needed before it's tension rather than a swing-y gotcha?

SCOPE / SOLO-FEASIBILITY: this is effectively a new game on an existing engine (new factions, art, three cross-coupled systems, balance, onboarding). The realistic failure is unfinished design, not bad design. Is the right first ship even smaller than 6 factions — e.g. 3-4 sharply differentiated blocs + ONE new cross-coupled system (territory+attrition economy) done well — to prove the thesis before broadening?

RANKED 1v1 vs the full hybrid: diplomacy/minors are recommended OFF on the competitive ladder, but does that fork the game into two balance problems (a lean competitive mode and a rich skirmish/FFA mode), and which one is the primary customer the whole design should optimize for?
design.detail:
SYNTHESIS LOGIC (how the 9 research dimensions resolve into one opinionated design): The psychology and hybrids dimensions agree on the central thesis and it drives everything — the current loop is shallow because it is SOLVED (one dominant line), not because it lacks systems, and 'add diplomacy+research+economy' is a coin flip decided by whether each addition produces non-dominated, cross-coupled, interesting decisions (depth) or just more menus and clicks (complexity). Rise of Nations is the explicit north star (it shipped almost exactly this vision: real-time, 20-60min, ages, library research, borders, attrition, rare strategic resources, simple diplomacy, 18 asymmetric nations), Company of Heroes is the secondary lens (territory=economy, low-unit-count high-decision-density, comeback mechanics), Sins donates UI-at-scale and positive-incentive diplomacy but its hours-long tempo is explicitly REJECTED, and Stellaris/Civ are the cautionary DON'Ts (parallel size-scaling micromanagement, slow resource-accumulation gates, snowball). The one-line framing the hybrids research recommends and I adopt: 'Rise of Nations' strategic systems expressed through Company of Heroes' territory-is-economy high-decision-density combat, kept to a single real-time layer, with Sins' overview UI and Supreme Commander's flow-economy automation to keep it fast.'

WHY EACH SYSTEM LANDS ON THE DEPTH SIDE OF THE LINE: the four 4X-lite systems are deliberately made to CROSS-COUPLE (economy gates research via strategic deposits; research/doctrine reshapes which diplomatic and defensive options exist; diplomacy over minors reshapes the contested map; the contested map IS the economy) so a few rules yield combinatorial depth — the Civ-vs-Stellaris distinction the psychology research identifies as the single highest-leverage lever. Each was independently designed by its specialist dimension to be fast and legible: research is 3 layers with a hard ~5-live-choice cap and a 'no invisible tax' lint rule; economy is 1+3+2 resources under the working-memory ceiling with educate-via-codex / gate-via-mechanic; defense is active cost-exchange with an explicit anti-stalemate ship checklist; diplomacy is 7 templated time-boxed one-click agreements with bribable minors solving the 'diplomacy is dead in 1v1' problem. The anti-spam dimension supplied the deathball cures (territory rewards spread, real top-unit vulnerabilities force composition, saturation drains finite magazines, research is opportunity-cost) and the countries dimension supplied the asymmetry-by-strategic-use roster with paired strength/weakness balancing.

ENGINE FEASIBILITY (from the feasibility dimension, verified in-repo): ~70% of this is data-only mod work (factions, units, balance, eras/doctrines/upgrades as MiniYAML prerequisites + conditions + support powers), ~25% modest new C# traits, ~5% engine glue. The mature systems used as-is: TechTree/ProvidesPrerequisite/Buildable (prerequisite graph, live as actors change), SupportPower + prerequisites (superweapons slot into the tech tree for free), GainsExperience (veterancy), FactionInfo + Buildable.ForceFaction (per-faction unique units), JamsMissiles/AmmoPool/DetectCloaked/GrantExternalConditionWarhead/Mine (defense primitives), the Encyclopedia widget (Codex). The genuinely NEW C# is small and well-scoped: (1) a DiplomacyManager + SetRelationship synced order mutating AlliedPlayersMask/EnemyPlayersMask (the ONLY relationship code missing — masks are currently set once at init in CreateMapPlayers.SetupPlayerMasks and never changed; ~250 LOC) plus a MinorFaction trait on ProximityCapturable; (2) a ResearchQueue trait modeled on ProductionQueue (integer cost/tick, [Sync]) emitting prerequisite/condition tokens; (3) a thin PlayerStrategicResources counter cloned from PlayerResources + a generalized GrantConditionOnPlayerResources for stockpile-gated tech; (4) a PointDefense trait extending JamsMissiles' chance pattern (finite AmmoPool + per-shot credit cost + visible pips) and a CounterBattery trait; (5) Food/Water as a second PowerManager-pattern meter. DETERMINISM is the #1 risk class and binds every new trait reachable from world.Tick(): integer/fixed-point only (WPos/WDist/WAngle, no float/double/DateTime), all RNG via the synced MersenneTwister (never System.Random), all mutable diplomatic/research/defense state [Sync], every relationship change through a synced order — the CheckSyncAnnotations lint and make check catch most violations. The supply-line/convoy economy, territory ownership, and per-tick interception all run in the sim tick and must obey this.

ART IS THE TRUE COST CEILING (every dimension flags it): 32-facing sprites per unit means a wrong systemic bet is expensive to unwind, so the whole program is sequenced cheap-to-change (systems in YAML/Lua with recolored/placeholder art) BEFORE expensive-to-change (bespoke art), with art commissioning gated by proven fun. The hybrid Blender-render + AI-single-angle pipeline, the shared base set + 12 hero sprites scoping, and the vertical-slice-first rollout all serve this. The recommended build order: PHASE 1 prove the core loop (territory-economy + 1 strategic stockpile + dynamic diplomacy order, art-free/recolored, 2-3 blocs) and run the decision-density/no-dominant-strategy/automate-tedium playtest gates; PHASE 2 add doctrine-research + the defense interception/EW layer; PHASE 3 add minors + the radial UI + the remaining stockpiles; PHASE 4 commission the vertical-slice art for the proven factions and expand to 6 then 12 blocs. Fun is treated as an engineering constraint with explicit metric gates, not hoped for.
